What Ukrainian young people are going through today is a challenging experience: nights spent in bomb shelters, studying during air raid alerts, volunteering after Russian attacks, playing sports on destroyed grounds, defending Ukraine on the battlefield, enduring the hellish Russian captivity, and facing countless other hardships brought upon Ukrainians by Russia’s war. On International Youth Day, we reiterate: Ukrainian youth deserve a peaceful future where they will no longer need to know how to distinguish the sounds of Russian drones and missiles. Ukrainians who are held in Russian captivity today must be released without delay. All Ukrainian kids whose childhood and youth have been stolen by Russia’s unlawful deportation must be brought home. Eternal memory to the young Ukrainians who gave their lives defending our freedom. Their courage and sacrifice will forever remain part of Ukraine’s history. Despite all these challenges, Ukrainian young people are already taking responsibility for their country’s future. They are indeed the future of Ukraine – a future worth fighting for.

Every parent wants to keep their children safe, and vaccines are among the most powerful tools for doing that, making deadly diseases preventable. @WHO is concerned that recent changes to US immunization policy are not aligned with decades of evidence that show when children are most vulnerable to disease, when vaccines provide the strongest protection, how many doses are needed, and which vaccines can be given together safely. That evidence is reviewed continuously as new data emerge from across the globe. The current evidence is unequivocal: vaccines - including the MMR vaccine - are safe and do not cause autism. Delaying vaccines or separating doses unnecessarily does not make vaccination safer and can leave children unprotected. Global evidence and recommendations, including from @WHO, inform national experts, who consider local disease patterns, health systems and population needs, to determine which vaccines and schedules are best for their country. Vaccination policy should be guided by rigorous, independent and transparent review of the best available science, not by political influence.

At the 2026 Conference on Hongshan Culture, Guo Zhan, former vice-president of the International Council on Monuments and Sites, highlighted in his speech that world heritage designation is not about "protecting all that can be protected". Rather, sites must be evaluated within the global context of human civilization to select the best of the best. He noted that world heritage recognition rests on three key pillars: outstanding universal value, authenticity and integrity, and protection and management. For the Hongshan culture, archaeological sites serve as "physical historical documents" carrying rich historical information, with authenticity acting as an indispensable pillar. The ultimate core of heritage conservation is to permanently pass down a site's value as a historical witness, a source of guidance, and an aesthetic treasure to future generations. #HongshanCulture #CulturalJourney Video

#WATCH | Delhi: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju says, "I am totally frustrated. For the first time in my life, I am witnessing a scenario where the government wants a discussion in Parliament, yet the opposition is running away from it. It is hard to imagine this, because in a parliamentary democracy, it is the opposition that demands a discussion while the government provides the answers. Here, however, the government itself is saying, we will hold a discussion and provide answers, but the opposition refuses to listen. Can you imagine such a situation? It is not good for democracy. We have repeatedly stated our willingness to discuss the matter, yet they refuse to agree. Consequently, the Home Minister was compelled to write another letter, the Home Minister wrote to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, reiterating that we are ready for an open, extensive, and detailed discussion and asking him to persuade the opposition leaders to agree to it. Have you ever heard of such a thing? The government itself is earnestly requesting the Speaker to convince the opposition to participate in a discussion. Even today, we repeatedly urged the opposition to start the discussion right away but they simply lack the courage. This is not good for the country..." Video

GUR tells @mil_in_ua that Russia is producing 3,000 jet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 as well as up to 80 Banderol missiles per month. militarnyi.com/uk/news/3-tys… militarnyi.com/uk/news/rosiy… Rob Lee (@RALee85) Another useful interview with Deputy Chief of Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence Major General Vadym Skibitskyi. Some highlights: -Russia increased ballistic missile production by suspending production of Kinzhal and Kh-32, both of which have accuracy problems (greater than 30 meter deviation). -"Another example is Russia’s planned production of strike drones for August this year – Geran-1, Geran-2, Geran-3, Geran-4, Geran-5, Garpiya, Gerbera, Gerbera kamikaze and Gerbera seeker drones – 11,000 units in total." -"In July, they slightly reduced the intensity of their drone strikes and cut production as they reconfigure their manufacturing capacity, with a focus on turbojet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones. In one of their recent attacks, turbojet-powered drones already accounted for 50% of the total. We now need different interceptors capable of matching their speed, or short-range air defense systems." -"According to estimates by Ukraine's Defense Intelligence, July ranked second after February in the number of Kh-101, Kalibr and Kh-32 cruise missiles launched. In February, the Russians launched 157 such missiles at us, while in July they launched 153." -"As for ballistic and hypersonic missiles – the 9M723 missiles used by the Iskander-M system, the RM-48U missiles launched from S-400 systems, and Zircon missiles – the enemy launched 198 of them in July. That is the highest figure this year." -"In the first seven months of this year, they had already produced 33 Zircon missiles, according to data as of August 3. The same applies to Onyx missiles: as of August 3, they had produced 60 units." -"Overall, across the main types of missile weapons, Russia is currently exceeding its monthly production targets by 110-120%. According to intelligence, Russia’s July production target for Kh-101 missiles was met at 140%, for Kalibr missiles at 111%, and for Kh-35 cruise missiles at 200%. -"Russia’s August production target for Kh-101 missiles is 72 units. The target was the same in July, but they produced more – 87 missiles. For the 3M14 Kalibr, the August target is 26 units. The July target was also 26, but they produced 29." -"According to military intelligence, as of August 5, the stockpile allocated to the Russian military grouping stood at around 130 9M723 missiles. The planned monthly production rate is 60 units. However, in July, they produced 65 instead of the planned 60." -"They are not really drawing down their stockpiles. Almost everything being used now is coming straight off the production line. The only exception is the Kalibr missiles - most of them are currently being allocated to other Russian fleets, since all new Russian warships and submarines are equipped with these systems. "The jade dragon of Hongshan culture marks another round of long-distance prehistoric jade diffusion in China, following the southward spread of Northeast Asian jue rings." At the 2026 Conference on Hongshan Culture, Fang Xiangming, director and research fellow at the Zhejiang Provincial Institute of Cultural Relics and Archaeology, shared his research on the spread and evolution of the Hongshan jade dragon. He stated that the Hongshan jade dragon spread over 1,500 kilometers to the lower Yangtze region, eventually becoming part of the deity figure, the unified emblem of Liangzhu belief. Reaching 1,500 kilometers away to the Taihu Lake Basin, this transmission spread three-dimensional carving techniques and beliefs. Beyond borrowing artistic motifs and forms, it reflects a shared mythological belief. The Hongshan and Liangzhu cultures are the earliest and most systematic models in the heritage and innovation of Chinese jade culture, forming essential pillars of China's 5,000-year civilization. #HongshanCulture #CulturalJourney Video

অস্ট্রেলিয়ার বিপক্ষে দুই ম্যাচের টেস্ট সিরিজ দিয়ে দীর্ঘ অপেক্ষার অবসান ঘটাতে যাচ্ছে বাংলাদেশ।বৃহস্পতিবার (১৩ আগস্ট) ডারউইনের মারারা স্টেডিয়ামে শুরু হবে সিরিজের প্রথম টেস্ট। বিশ্ব টেস্ট চ্যাম্পিয়নশিপের অংশ হওয়ায় ম্যাচ পরিচালনার দায়িত্বে থাকছেন আইসিসির অভিজ্ঞ ও শীর্ষস্থানীয় ম্যাচ অফিসিয়ালরা। প্রথম টেস্টে অন-ফিল্ড আম্পায়ারের দায়িত্বে থাকবেন ইংল্যান্ডের রিচার্ড ইলিংওর্থ ও শ্রীলঙ্কার কুমার ধর্মসেনা। তৃতীয় আম্পায়ার হিসেবে থাকবেন ভারতের নীতিন মেনন। চতুর্থ আম্পায়ারের দায়িত্ব পালন করবেন অস্ট্রেলিয়ার স্যাম নোগাজস্কি। ম্যাচ রেফারি হিসেবে থাকবেন রিচার্ড রিচার্ডসন। ২২ আগস্ট ম্যাকাইয়ের গ্রেট ব্যারিয়ার রিফ এরেনায় শুরু হবে সিরিজের দ্বিতীয় ও শেষ টেস্ট। সেখানে অন-ফিল্ড আম্পায়ার হিসেবে দায়িত্ব পালন করবেন নীতিন মেনন ও কুমার ধর্মসেনা। তৃতীয় আম্পায়ার থাকবেন ইলিংওর্থ এবং চতুর্থ আম্পায়ার দোনোভান কচ। ম্যাচ রেফারি হিসেবে থাকবেন রিচার্ডসনই। ২০০৩ সালের পর এবারই প্রথম অস্ট্রেলিয়ার মাটিতে টেস্ট খেলবে বাংলাদেশ। প্রস্তুতি ম্যাচে ক্রিকেট অস্ট্রেলিয়া একাদশের কাছে ইনিংস ব্যবধানে হারায় সফরকারীদের আত্মবিশ্বাসে কিছুটা ধাক্কা লেগেছে। অন্যদিকে, বিশ্ব টেস্ট চ্যাম্পিয়নশিপের গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পয়েন্ট হাতছাড়া করতে না চেয়ে পূর্ণ শক্তির দল নিয়ে মাঠে নামছে অস্ট্রেলিয়া। #cricket #cricketnews #NewsUpdate #somoytv

V inspiring … Ajai Chowdhry (@AjaiChowdhry) We quit our jobs. There were six of us — Shiv Nadar, Arjun Malhotra, Yogesh Vaidya, Subhash Arora, D.S. Puri and me. It was 1976. Startups were not really a thing in India. Venture capital did not exist. Banks were not exactly lining up to lend money to six young men with an idea and no collateral. And computers? Most people had barely heard of them. But we believed the microprocessor was going to change the world. So we took the plunge. Between the six of us, we managed to put together ₹1.87 lakh. We borrowed, pooled our savings and, in one case, even sold a car. Our first office was a small barsati in Golf Links, Delhi. We called ourselves Microcomp. We wanted to build an Indian computer. There was just one problem. We didn’t have a manufacturing licence. That eventually led us to UP Electronics Corporation. They had the licence. We had the technology. And that partnership gave birth to Hindustan Computers Limited — HCL. But perhaps the most audacious part of the story was what happened next. We started selling a computer that was still being designed. We had a brochure and a mock-up of the machine. That was it. Our sales teams went across India, knocking on doors and convincing businesses to buy into a technology they had never used before. The first orders came from IIT Kharagpur and IIT Madras. Then came the harder part — convincing businesses. In Coimbatore, we were up against DCM DP, a much bigger and more established name. I still remember sitting in the reception area of Premier Mills while the DCM team made its pitch. We went in second. And we won. That one order gave us five more. Then ten. That was HCL in those early years: not having the biggest balance sheet, the biggest brand or the easiest path — but finding a way. We were restless. We looked for gaps. We hired people who had what we called a “cowboy” spirit. We believed that technology had to be made useful and accessible, not intimidating. And we kept moving. From building India’s early indigenous computers to taking our business to Singapore when HCL was just four years old. From a small room in Delhi to a global technology company. When I look back at 50 years, I think about six people sitting together in 1976, wondering if this crazy idea could actually work. I think about a barsati. A brochure for a computer that did not yet exist. And the courage to knock on the next door. That, to me, is the real HCL story. 50 years later, the technology has changed beyond anything we could have imagined. But the spirit remains the same: Dream big. Take the risk. I was highly skeptical of the very enthusiastic and open support for #Yabloko in the upcoming Duma elections from virtually all the Russian opposition in exile. First of all, “elections” is far too strong a word for this process. Secondly, there is no doubt that only the Presidential Administration decides who appears on the ballot. Yabloko’s participation therefore served a clear purpose in the eyes of Russian political managers. Simulation of normality. Thirdly, there was never any question that Yabloko was not aiming for a “revolution in the Duma.” It was simply trying to secure its continued niche while accepting the overall rules of the game. Yesterday a court barred them from the elections altogether. Now many voices are “blaming” the Russian opposition in exile for supporting Yabloko too openly and thereby provoking an angry reaction inside Russia. It turns out (see the link for detailed @RiddleRussia on this in the first comment) that it was not the émigrés who made the difference, but Russians inside Russia itself. The moment Yabloko stepped out of the shadows and announced it would participate in the elections under anti-war slogans, interest among Russians surged surpassing the ruling United Russia figure despite heavy paid promotion of United Russia on all platforms. This does not mean Yabloko would have won a majority in free and fair elections just like that. But running on a simple “stop the war” platform would almost certainly have let them aim for second place with relatively little effort. Based on this promise alone. The Presidential Administration simply did not anticipate such a sharp surge of interest—or the potential catastrophe it posed for their carefully staged “nice results.” Upsetting Putin is too much of a risk. That is why Yabloko was banned.

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif's Message on International Youth Day 12 August 2026. Pakistan joins the international community in observing International Youth Day and pays tribute to our talented youth for their immense potential, vibrant energy, and positive aspirations. This year, International Youth Day is being observed under the theme “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations.” The theme duly underscores the fact that although the lives of young people across the world are shaped by diverse circumstances, their dreams, aspirations, and hopes for a brighter future remain remarkably similar. Our youth are an invaluable National asset and are the promising driving force for our bright future. The creativity and determined efforts of our young people are undoubtedly contributing to encouraging progress across every sector of society. Harnessing the potential and capabilities of our youth is essential for building a prosperous, peaceful, and strong Pakistan. Pakistan’s young population has brought laurels to the country at both the national and international levels through their achievements across various fields of life. At the local level too, our youth are playing a constructive role as active members of society. Ensuring the best possible intellectual, physical, mental, and academic development of our youth through the effective utilization of all available national resources remains among the Government’s key priorities. The Government of Pakistan is committed to empowering our youth through modern and quality education aligned with the demands of the day, through dedicated efforts to promote technical and vocational skills, employment opportunities, entrepreneurship, industrial development, digital innovation, and social inclusion. Alongside various policy initiatives, the Government is also taking practical measures enabling young people to align their abilities, skills, and professional competencies with international standards so to make the country proud on the global stage. To provide talented students with opportunities to advance in education, information technology, technical fields, and artificial intelligence, the Government has taken several important initiatives, including scholarship programmes, laptop distribution, and paid internships for students. Furthermore, the Prime Minister’s Youth Skill Development Programme (PMYSDP) is striving to ensure a talented and skilled workforce in the country. The National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NAVTTC) has been further strengthened on a priority basis to provide internationally recognized certifications and world-class training in professional and technical skills.The national institution is taking special measures to equip the workforce with internationally recognized qualifications and the skills required by industries. On this day, I have a special message for our youth: continue your journey of hard work with honesty, responsibility, and a spirit of service to the nation. The sustainable development and bright future of our country are intrinsically linked to the progress of our youth. Let us renew our resolve to work together with full commitment and play a constructive and active role in the development and prosperity of our country, so that our homeland becomes a guarantee of a bright future for all segments of society especially our youth.

Prof. K.V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, along with officials from NITI Aayog, visited Telangana from 05–07 August 2026 to engage with the State Government on key development priorities. During the visit, Prof. Raju held discussions with the Chief Secretary and senior officials of the State Government. He emphasised the need for adopting a uniform methodology for estimating District Domestic Product (DDP) and Primary Sector GDP to enable consistent assessment and support evidence-based decision-making at the district level. Detailed deliberations were also held on advancing the State’s implementation strategy for achieving the objectives outlined in the Vision Document and establishing an institutional mechanism for regular review of progress and resolution of implementation challenges. Prof. Raju also visited sites showcasing some of Telangana’s best practices, including initiatives under the National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), innovative horticulture farming practices, and the development of Genome Valley as a leading biotechnology and life sciences hub in India. The visit further strengthened the partnership between NITI Aayog and the Government of Telangana and reaffirmed the shared commitment to translating the State’s development priorities into a strategic roadmap towards the goals of Viksit Bharat by 2047. #Telangana #CooperativeFederalism @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

Bloomberg said satellite imagery captured 12 ship-to-ship transfers off Oman and the UAE on Monday, indicating that tankers continue crossing with their tracking systems disabled. At least 4 outbound supertankers (VLCCs) carrying a combined 8 million barrels of crude have reappeared after transiting Hormuz since Saturday. Many vessels are hugging Oman’s coastline and receiving U.S. military assistance, allowing millions of barrels per day to leave the Persian Gulf and helping contain oil prices. Brent crude traded above $90 on Tuesday, before settling at $88.91 per barrel. But few tankers are entering to replace those leaving. ADNOC says 15 of its vessels have been attacked during the war. The limited number of shipowners willing to enter the Gulf has pushed benchmark tanker earnings close to $500,000 per day and ADNOC’s shipping arm reported sharply higher quarterly earnings from elevated freight rates and additional export services. Analyst Brett Erickson told Drop Site that outbound vessels are outnumbering inbound vessels by roughly 3.5 to one. That means the system is drawing down the finite pool of tankers already inside the Gulf. Without enough empty ships returning, he believes the storage will fill, causing production to be shut in, and making current export levels to become impossible to sustain. “This is buying time,” Erickson said. @ryangrim | @BrettErickson28 | @MazMHussain Video

Bloomberg said satellite imagery captured 12 ship-to-ship transfers off Oman and the UAE on Monday, indicating that tankers continue crossing with their tracking systems disabled. At least 4 outbound supertankers (VLCCs) carrying a combined 8 million barrels of crude have reappeared after transiting Hormuz since Saturday. Many vessels are hugging Oman’s coastline and receiving U.S. military assistance, allowing millions of barrels per day to leave the Persian Gulf and helping contain oil prices. Brent crude traded above $90 on Tuesday, before settling at $88.91 per barrel. But few tankers are entering to replace those leaving. ADNOC says 15 of its vessels have been attacked during the war. The limited number of shipowners willing to enter the Gulf has pushed benchmark tanker earnings close to $500,000 per day and ADNOC’s shipping arm reported sharply higher quarterly earnings from elevated freight rates and additional export services. Analyst Brett Erickson told Drop Site that outbound vessels are outnumbering inbound vessels by roughly 3.5 to one. That means the system is drawing down the finite pool of tankers already inside the Gulf. Without enough empty ships returning, he believes the storage will fill, causing production to be shut in, and making current export levels to become impossible to sustain. “This is buying time,” Erickson said. @ryangrim | @BrettErickson28 | @MazMHussain Video

Israel is entering a new “robotic age” in warfare, accelerating lessons learned from Gaza and Lebanon, where tens of thousands of unmanned and remotely operated systems have already been deployed. Under the IDF’s 2026 to 2030 Hoshen Plan, robotics, AI and autonomous systems will become central to force building across land, air and sea. The IDF is also establishing dedicated structures for robotics and autonomous warfare. Over the next decade, Israel plans to expand robotic systems for tunnel operations, reconnaissance, logistics, route clearance and combat. Older armored vehicles are also being converted into remotely operated platforms, while drone and ground robot swarms are being developed. The longer term goal is mixed human machine formations, with robotic systems moving ahead of soldiers and taking on the most dangerous battlefield missions while humans retain oversight of lethal decisions.

China Begins Shipping Goods to Europe via the Northern Sea Route Important news for global trade: China is launching the first regular container route through the Arctic waters of the Northern Sea Route. In recent years, the melting ice has made such shipments very promising. It is expected that ships from China will reach Europe in just 20 days, compared to 40 days via the southern route through the Suez Canal. Furthermore, this traditional route is not entirely safe today. What are the benefits for us? First, Russia, thanks to its geographical location and the world's most powerful icebreaker fleet, is the only country capable of ensuring the passage of maritime convoys along the NSR. Therefore, it has every right to charge for transit. The funds raised can be used to develop the Russian Arctic region, including military facilities for its defense. Many experts predict that in the near future, there will be competition between Russia and other Arctic states for the region's resources. We need to prepare for this struggle in advance. Second, the Northern Sea Route is the shortest and safest trade route between Russia and its largest trading partner, China, as well as with other countries in the region that maintain economic ties with Moscow. For European companies engaging in maritime piracy, our ships in the Arctic remain inaccessible. Again, this is because we have many icebreakers, while they have very few. And it's also a bit scary to engage in piracy under the sights of Russian "Bal" and "Bastion" systems. Third, the launch of regular commercial shipments enhances the prestige of Russia and China, which are visibly creating an alternative to the long-established logistics of international maritime trade. This is an element of the multipolar world that Vladimir Putin has spoken about repeatedly. Want to transport goods from Europe to Asia faster? Pay a visit to Moscow and Beijing. And they will take it from there. Of course, we shouldn't get ahead of ourselves. The NSR remains a seasonal and technically challenging route. If the ice conditions, insurance costs, sanctions, and the cost of icebreaker escort turn out to be higher than expected, carriers will use it as a niche or crisis route, rather than as a full-fledged alternative to the Suez Canal. Therefore, there is still a lot of work to be done to unlock the full potential of the Northern Sea Route. @sashakots

Daily Ukraine map thread for Tuesday 11th August 2026 A full focus today on the Lyman to Kupiansk front along the Kharkiv/Luhansk border, where, remarkably, both sides remain broadly matched and the map has displayed all the dynamism of a particularly stubborn brick wall. Much has been made of the 3rd Army Corps’ OPSEC north of Lyman, accompanied by the usual imaginative reporting about vast offensives which, like most vast offensives announced on Telegram, appear to exist primarily in the imagination. The relative silence tells rather more. Ukraine has achieved a partial success in relieving pressure around Lyman, where Russian infiltrators had previously managed to make things distinctly uncomfortable. But the other half of the job - actually cutting the salient - has not happened yet. And we should remember just how slowly this particular war moves. This sector has been in "quiet mode" for months. The area in question is sufficiently compact that a reasonably determined man could walk across much of it in about three hours, assuming he wasn't being shot at, which does rather spoil a nice walk. Yet after months, there is still no meaningful encirclement. At this pace, you simply aren't cutting off significant numbers of troops. You are giving them plenty of time to wander away, bring their belongings, and probably leave a forwarding address. That doesn't mean the Ukrainian effort has been pointless. Ukrainian losses appear to have remained relatively low, some ground has been recovered, Russian pressure around Lyman has been reduced, and perhaps most importantly, the Ukrainians have gained valuable experience conducting offensive operations. That last point matters enormously. Offensive experience is precisely the sort of thing Ukrainian forces have been painfully short of, and unlike territory, it cannot be measured neatly on a map. Further north, however, Russia has spent the year consolidating its positions. Russian forces are once again operating in Kupiansk and Kupiansk Vuzlovyi. For the moment, this isn't necessarily catastrophic. But it creates the ingredients for another attempt at taking the city. And this time, Russia may have learned from its previous performance. Last year, Russian forces appeared rather keen to declare premature victory in Kupiansk, at which point the Ukrainians enthusiastically demonstrated the disadvantages of premature celebration by killing a considerable number of them and clearing the city. This time the Russians hold additional positions on the eastern side of the Oskil, giving them a much better platform from which to infiltrate and pressure the city. So, for now, the Lyman to Kupiansk sector remains a curious combination of tactical activity and strategic inertia. In other words, after months of fighting over an area you could cross on foot in an afternoon, everyone remains remarkably close to where they started.

Hello everyone, I am starting a new fundraiser to help maintain and repair engineering equipment @LibertyUkraineF has already delivered to Ukraine with your aid. Donation link at the end of this post. Please read till the end, like, share and quote - it is very important for this fundraiser. Donations are tax deductible. Over the past 3 years, we have delivered more than 30 excavators, 40 heavy trucks, and loads of other engineering equipment such as cranes, augers, and off-road forklifts. 90% of the equipment we have delivered has performed exceptionally well, as we picked some of the most durable models. However, even the best equipment can't live forever, and the stress it's been put through on the battlefield shows. For example, one of the machines worked 12,000 hours over two years. That machine was a Yanmar VIO50 excavator that we bought, delivered, and serviced for $30,000. A new machine like this costs around $100,000. 12,000 machine hours is more than the expected lifetime of an excavator in this class. Today, this excavator returned to us for major repairs. I can't stress enough the importance of the work this machine performed. It served in the 43rd Artillery Brigade, building fortifications for PzH 2000 howitzers and digging trenches for drone pilots. It saved countless lives from drone threats and tens of millions of dollars in equipment by protecting critical assets. Today, we have a backlog of around 8 similar machines awaiting repairs. These machines have complex hydraulics, pins, and joints that require special equipment and expertise to repair. My goal has always been to deliver the best-value solutions for the least amount of funding. For example, a machine used to bore pin seats on an excavator costs around $15,000. We didn't have that kind of funding dedicated to repairs, so my brother @vaycartana built and programmed such a tool himself, and it cost us only $4,000. However, our ingenuity and desire to help Ukraine can only go so far without funding. We need parts, we need to pay for electricity, and we need to pay something to the workers who perform these repairs. This is back-breaking labor done under constant air raids, bombings, and air raid sirens. That's why I am asking you to donate to the fundraiser using the link at the end of this post. Our goal is to raise $30,000 to allow us to repair up to 6 excavators. Please share, quote repost, and like this post. Iran is adapting its tactics to wear down U.S. air defenses, and exploit dwindling interceptor stocks, according to new reporting from The New York Times. During five days of attacks on U.S. bases in Jordan last month, Iran combined drones with maneuvering ballistic missiles to overwhelm defensive systems. On July 17, one missile penetrated the defenses at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, killing 3 U.S. soldiers and wounding more than 100. The scale of the expenditure is becoming increasingly important: the U.S. has fired more than 1,500 Patriot interceptors during the war and reportedly has fewer than 1,700 remaining, while producing only about 600 Patriots in all of 2025. On one day during the Jordan attacks, U.S. forces reportedly fired around 50 Patriots, at roughly $4 million each. Iran has also demonstrated other adaptations, including using drones to provide targeting data that helped shoot down a U.S. F-15E in April and expanding attacks through partners such as the Houthis to force U.S. forces to defend against threats from multiple directions. The Pentagon continues to publicly deny that the U.S. has a munitions shortage.

The FAA is already spending billions to replace aging air-traffic-control telecommunications and radar infrastructure following a series of outages and failures.

Some maps help you find your way. Others help you see the world differently. 🗺️🎨 Our 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) captures the shape of the land through high-resolution elevation data. Through our 3DEP as Art series, we transform these scientific datasets into visual representations of elevation, revealing the ridges, valleys, and slopes that shape the terrain. Created from bare-earth elevation data, these maps remove vegetation and structures to showcase the underlying terrain in a new way. This data supports a wide range of applications, including mapping, natural resource management, hazard assessment, scientific research, and informed decision-making. They demonstrate how science, technology, and creativity can come together to provide new ways to explore and understand our surroundings. Science provides the data. Art reveals the landscape. President Donald Trump has announced the release of former U.S. Marine Robert Gilman, who has been imprisoned in Russia since 2022, saying the decision came after his discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Gilman was originally sentenced to 4 1/2 years after being convicted of assaulting a Russian police officer, but his sentence was later extended after additional allegations involving prison officials. His family and U.S. advocates have disputed aspects of the case. His release comes after serious deterioration in his health. Recent reports said Gilman had been hospitalized and had spent weeks in a dissociative state, prompting increased pressure from U.S. officials for Moscow to release him on humanitarian grounds. According to Trump, Russia released Gilman without a prisoner exchange or other concessions, describing it as a humanitarian decision following his discussions with Putin. U.S. officials likewise characterized the release as a goodwill gesture rather than a negotiated swap. Gilman is now returning to the United States for medical treatment.

On Tuesday, the Chief Minister held a review of the Metro Rail – old city project with senior officials of the Hyderabad Metro Rail Limited (HMRL). CM Revanth Reddy enquired the officials about the pending land acquisition and instructed them to finalise the Metro expansion plans immediately. Noting the steadily increasing ridership on the Hyderabad Metro, the Chief Minister emphasized appropriate measures to handle the passenger load including adding extra coaches to the trains and directed officials to procure the necessary additional metro rail coaches. Internet shutdowns can be brief, or months-long. No matter their duration, the impact lasts much longer. GCC क्षेत्रात महाराष्ट्राचे नेतृत्व, 400 केंद्रे आणि 4 लाख उच्च कौशल्याधारित रोजगारांचे लक्ष्य मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी आज पुणे येथे 'जीसीसीप्रोस लीडरशिप समिट' येथे प्रमुख उपस्थिती दर्शवली. महाराष्ट्राला जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांसाठी (जीसीसी) भारतातील आघाडीचे आणि सर्वाधिक पसंतीचे ठिकाण बनविण्याचा राज्य सरकारचा निर्धार असून, राज्यात 400 नवीन जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रे, 4,00,000 उच्च कौशल्याधारित रोजगाराच्या संधी आणि ₹50,000 कोटींची गुंतवणूक आकर्षित करण्याचे महत्त्वाकांक्षी उद्दिष्ट निश्चित करण्यात आले आहे, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी प्रतिपादन केले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, भारतातील जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांच्या वाटचालीची सुरुवात कुशल मनुष्यबळ, कौशल्य आणि खर्चाच्या दृष्टीने कार्यक्षमतेच्या आधारे झाली. मात्र, आता या क्षेत्राचे स्वरूप मोठ्या प्रमाणात बदलत आहे. 2030 मधील जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रे केवळ कार्यालयीन सहाय्यक कामकाजापुरती मर्यादित राहणार नाहीत, ती अभियांत्रिकी, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता, उत्पादन विकास, सायबर सुरक्षा, वित्तीय सेवा, माहिती विश्लेषण तसेच संशोधन व विकासाची केंद्रे बनतील. या केंद्रांमधून जागतिक व्यवसायांचे महत्त्वपूर्ण निर्णयही घेतले जातील, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. महाराष्ट्राकडे सर्वसमावेशक परिसंस्था मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, महाराष्ट्राला जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांच्या क्षेत्रात मोठी आघाडी मिळवून देणारे वैशिष्ट्य म्हणजे या केंद्रांसाठी आवश्यक असलेली सर्वसमावेशक परिसंस्था राज्यात आधीपासूनच उपलब्ध आहे. मुंबईकडे देशातील सखोल वित्तीय व व्यावसायिक परिसंस्था आहे. पुण्याकडे अभियांत्रिकी, वाहन उद्योग, उत्पादन क्षेत्र, तंत्रज्ञान आणि गुणवत्तापूर्ण मनुष्यबळाचा मजबूत आधार आहे. नाशिक, नागपूर आणि छत्रपती संभाजीनगर यांसारख्या शहरांमध्येही जागतिक क्षमतेची विशेषीकृत केंद्रे विकसित करण्याची क्षमता आहे. त्यामुळे महाराष्ट्रात केवळ एका शहरात गुंतवणूक करण्याची संधी नसून, विविध शहरांमध्ये उपलब्ध असलेल्या प्रतिभा, कौशल्य आणि औद्योगिक क्षमतांचा एकत्रित लाभ घेण्याची संधी आहे. पुण्याने 2025 मध्ये जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांच्या क्षेत्रातील आपली योग्यता सिद्ध केली आहे. 2025 मध्ये पुणे भारतातील दुसऱ्या क्रमांकाची मोठी जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांची कार्यालयीन बाजारपेठ ठरली असून, मागील वर्षाच्या तुलनेत या केंद्रांसाठीच्या कार्यालयीन जागेच्या मागणीत दुपटीहून अधिक वाढ झाली आहे. 2026 च्या अखेरीस जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांच्या क्षेत्रात पुणे देशाचे नेतृत्व करेल, असा विश्वास मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी व्यक्त केला. केवळ अनुदान नव्हे, सक्षम परिसंस्था निर्माण करण्यावर भर मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, केवळ आर्थिक सवलतींच्या बळावर GCC आकर्षित करणे हे शासनाचे उद्दिष्ट नाही. दीर्घकाळ टिकणारी परिसंस्था प्रतिभावान मनुष्यबळ, पायाभूत सुविधा, व्यवसाय सुलभता, उत्तम जीवनमान, संशोधन, विद्यापीठे, दळणवळण आणि शासन-उद्योगातील विश्वासाच्या भक्कम आधारावर उभी राहते. राज्याच्या जागतिक क्षमता केंद्र धोरणामध्ये वेतनावरील अनुदान, भांडवली खर्च किंवा भाड्यासाठी सहाय्य, व्याज अनुदान, संशोधन व विकासासाठी सहाय्य तसेच अन्य आर्थिक प्रोत्साहनांचा समावेश आहे. यासोबतच उद्योगाचा दर्जा, अतिरिक्त चटई क्षेत्र निर्देशांक (FSI), क्षेत्रवापरातील लवचिकता, जमिनीची प्राधान्याने उपलब्धता, डिजिटल माहिती संग्रह, विश्वासार्ह पायाभूत सुविधा आणि 24 तास, 7 ही दिवस कार्यपद्धतीसाठी आवश्यक सुविधा उपलब्ध करून देण्यावर भर देण्यात आला आहे. मात्र, ही सर्व साधने असून, खरे उद्दिष्ट क्षमता निर्माण करणे हे आहे, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी स्पष्ट केले. भविष्यातील कौशल्याधारित मनुष्यबळाची निर्मिती आवश्यक आज उद्योगांसमोर केवळ मनुष्यबळाची उपलब्धता नव्हे, तर भविष्यातील गरजांनुसार कुशल मनुष्यबळाची उपलब्धता सुनिश्चित करण्याचे आव्हान आहे. त्यामुळे भविष्यातील गरजा लक्षात घेऊन कुशल मनुष्यबळाची उपलब्धता साखळी निर्माण करणे आवश्यक आहे. कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्तेमुळे रोजगाराचे स्वरूप वेगाने बदलत आहे. कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता अभियंते, माहिती-विश्लेषण तज्ज्ञ, सायबर सुरक्षा तज्ज्ञ, अर्धवाहक तंत्रज्ञान अभियंते, उत्पादन व्यवस्थापक, प्रगत उत्पादन तंत्रज्ञान अभियंते, परिमाणात्मक वित्तीय क्षेत्रातील तज्ज्ञ आणि जीवविज्ञानविषयक तज्ज्ञ अशा विविध कौशल्यांची मागणी वाढत आहे. सरकार, उद्योग आणि शिक्षण क्षेत्राने एकत्रितपणे भविष्यातील कौशल्यांची निर्मिती करणे आवश्यक आहे. उद्योगांनी विद्यापीठांमध्ये भविष्यात कोणती कौशल्ये शिकवली जावीत, याबाबत मार्गदर्शन करावे. 5 वर्षांपूर्वी कोणती कौशल्ये आवश्यक होती, यापेक्षा पुढील 5 वर्षांत कोणती कौशल्ये आवश्यक असतील, हे उद्योगांनी सांगावे, असे आवाहनही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी केले. कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता आणि अत्याधुनिक तंत्रज्ञानात महाराष्ट्र आघाडीवर राहणार मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता क्षेत्रात महाराष्ट्राला आघाडीवर राहायचे आहे. यावर्षी दावोस येथे बीकेसी मध्ये 'कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता तंत्रज्ञानाच्या वापर, संशोधन आणि नवोन्मेषावर केंद्रित केंद्र' स्थापन करण्यासाठी सामंजस्य करार करण्यात आला आहे. भविष्यातील तंत्रज्ञानाच्या निर्मितीत महाराष्ट्राने महत्त्वाची भूमिका बजावावी, हा या उपक्रमामागील उद्देश आहे. अर्धवाहक तंत्रज्ञान, वित्तीय तंत्रज्ञान, सायबर सुरक्षा, प्रगत अभियांत्रिकी, औषधनिर्माण संशोधन व विकास, विद्युत वाहन तंत्रज्ञान आणि औद्योगिक तंत्रज्ञान या क्षेत्रांमध्ये महाराष्ट्राकडे आधीपासूनच भक्कम औद्योगिक क्षमता आहे. जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांची पुढील पिढी या क्षमतांच्या संगमावर विकसित झाली पाहिजे, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. मुंबई-पुण्यासोबतच अन्य शहरांमध्येही क्षमता केंद्रांचा विस्तार मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, राज्यातील सर्व 400 जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रे केवळ मुंबई-पुण्यापुरती मर्यादित न राहता, द्वितीय व तृतीय स्तरातील शहरांमध्येही विकसित झाली पाहिजेत. मुंबई, पुणे, नवी मुंबई, नागपूर, नाशिक आणि छत्रपती संभाजीनगर यांसारख्या शहरांमधील स्थानिक प्रतिभा व औद्योगिक क्षमतेनुसार विशेषीकृत जीसीसी विकसित केल्यास महाराष्ट्राची अधिक व्यापक आणि सक्षम जीसीसी परिसंस्था उभी राहील. मुंबई जागतिक वित्तीय आणि संस्थात्मक कार्यांचे केंद्र, पुणे अभियांत्रिकी व उत्पादन विकासाचे केंद्र, नवी मुंबई जागतिक व्यवसाय व तंत्रज्ञान केंद्र, नागपूर विशेषीकृत तंत्रज्ञान व सामायिक सेवा केंद्र, नाशिक अभियांत्रिकी व औद्योगिक क्षमतांचे केंद्र आणि छत्रपती संभाजीनगर प्रगत उत्पादन व वाहन उद्योगातील क्षमतांचे केंद्र म्हणून विकसित होऊ शकते, यामुळे अधिक व्यापक आणि लवचिक जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांची परिसंस्था निर्माण होईल, असेही मुख्यमंंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. शासनाच्या कार्यपद्धतीतही परिवर्तन करू मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांच्या क्षेत्रात परिवर्तन अपेक्षित असेल, तर शासनानेही आपल्या कार्यपद्धतीत परिवर्तन घडवून आणले पाहिजे. आजच्या वेगवान आणि सतत बदलणाऱ्या जगात शासनानेही संस्थेसारखे आणि व्यासपीठासारखे कार्य करणे आवश्यक आहे. उद्योगांना नियमित मंजुरीसाठी आठवडे किंवा महिने प्रतीक्षा करावी लागू नये. त्यांना निश्चितता, एक स्पष्ट उत्तर आणि समस्या निर्माण झाल्यास त्याची जबाबदारी स्वीकारणारी यंत्रणा मिळाली पाहिजे. जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांसाठी एकच जबाबदार सरकारी संपर्क व्यवस्था निर्माण करण्यासाठी राज्य सरकार काम करणार आहे. केंद्र स्थापन करणे, त्याचा विस्तार करणे आणि उद्भवणाऱ्या समस्या सोडविणे यासाठी 1 व्यक्ती आणि 1 प्रणाली जबाबदारी घेईल. व्यवसाय सुलभतेचा खरा अर्थ उद्योगांना शासनाच्या कार्यालयात येताना मिळणारा अनुभव सुधारण्यात आहे आणि तो अनुभव सुधारण्याचा शासनाचा निर्धार असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी नमूद केले. $1 ट्रिलियनच्या अर्थव्यवस्थेच्या उद्दिष्टात जीसीसीची महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका महाराष्ट्राला $1 ट्रिलियनची अर्थव्यवस्था बनविण्याच्या महत्त्वाकांक्षी उद्दिष्टात जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांची भूमिका अत्यंत महत्त्वाची आहे. ही केंद्रे केवळ भांडवल घेऊन येत नाहीत, तर ज्ञान, जागतिक कार्यपद्धती, संशोधन व विकास, नेतृत्व आणि उच्च मूल्याधारित रोजगार घेऊन येतात. महाराष्ट्रातील प्रतिभावान मनुष्यबळाला ही केंद्रे थेट जागतिक अर्थव्यवस्थेशी जोडतात आणि जागतिक पातळीवरील निर्णयक्षमतेचे सघन केंद्र निर्माण करतात. उद्योग, शासन आणि शिक्षण क्षेत्राच्या संयुक्त प्रयत्नातून महाराष्ट्राला जागतिक क्षमता केंद्रांसाठी भारतातील आघाडीचे आणि सर्वाधिक पसंतीचे ठिकाण बनविण्याचे आवाहनही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी केले. यावेळी उपमुख्यमंत्री सुनेत्रा अजित पवार, जीसीसीप्रोसचे मुख्य कार्यकारी अधिकारी शम्मी प्रभाकर सिंह, जीसीसीप्रोसचे सहसंस्थापक आणि समन्वयक नीलेश देशमुख व इतर मान्यवर उपस्थित होते. বাংলাদেশে নিযুক্ত ভারতের হাইকমিশনার দীনেশ ত্রিবেদী নয়াদিল্লিতে দেশটির প্রধানমন্ত্রী নরেন্দ্র মোদির সঙ্গে বৈঠক করেছেন। ঢাকায় প্রধানমন্ত্রী তারেক রহমানের সঙ্গে বৈঠকের একদিন পর আজ মঙ্গলবার (১১ আগস্ট) এ সাক্ষাৎ অনুষ্ঠিত হয়। নয়াদিল্লির একটি কূটনৈতিক সূত্রের বরাত দিয়ে ইউএনবি জানিয়েছে, বৈঠকে বাংলাদেশ-ভারত সম্পর্ক নিয়ে আলোচনা হয়েছে। সূত্রটি জানায়, ‘হ্যাঁ, তিনি আজ প্রধানমন্ত্রী নরেন্দ্র মোদির সঙ্গে বৈঠক করেছেন। তারা বাংলাদেশ-ভারত সম্পর্ক নিয়ে আলোচনা করেছেন।’ এর আগে ঢাকায় ধারাবাহিক তিনটি বৈঠক শেষে সোমবার (১০ আগস্ট) নয়াদিল্লি যান দীনেশ ত্রিবেদী। প্রতিবেশী দুই দেশের সম্পর্ককে আরও এগিয়ে নিতে গঠনমূলক যোগাযোগ ও চলমান কূটনৈতিক পরামর্শের অংশ হিসেবে এসব বৈঠককে দেখা হচ্ছে। রোববার রাষ্ট্রীয় অতিথি ভবন পদ্মায় বাংলাদেশের পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী ড. খলিলুর রহমানের সঙ্গে বৈঠক করেন ভারতীয় হাইকমিশনার। এরপর সোমবার সচিবালয়ে পৃথকভাবে প্রধানমন্ত্রী তারেক রহমান ও স্বরাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী সালাহউদ্দিন আহমেদের সঙ্গে বৈঠক করেন তিনি। প্রধানমন্ত্রী তারেক রহমানের সঙ্গে বৈঠকে দীনেশ ত্রিবেদী বাংলাদেশের সরকার ও জনগণের সঙ্গে ‘ইতিবাচক, গঠনমূলক ও ভবিষ্যতমুখী’ উপায়ে কাজ করার বিষয়ে ভারতের আগ্রহের কথা জানান। বৈঠকে দুই দেশের পারস্পরিক স্বার্থসংশ্লিষ্ট বিভিন্ন বিষয় নিয়ে মতবিনিময় হয়। পাশাপাশি জনগণকেন্দ্রিক দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিতে বাংলাদেশ-ভারত দ্বিপক্ষীয় সম্পর্ক আরও জোরদারের বিভিন্ন পথ নিয়েও আলোচনা করেন তারা। ঢাকায় ধারাবাহিক বৈঠকের পর ভারতীয় হাইকমিশনারের নয়াদিল্লি সফর এবং মোদির সঙ্গে তার বৈঠককে বাংলাদেশ-ভারত সম্পর্ক নিয়ে উচ্চপর্যায়ের চলমান যোগাযোগের অংশ হিসেবে দেখা হচ্ছে। #BangladeshIndia #NarendraModi #Diplomacy #somoytv

এ মাসের শেষদিকে বাংলাদেশ সফরে আসার কথা ছিল ভারতের। তবে রাজনৈতিক অস্থিরতার জেরে সেই সফর ঘিরে তৈরি হয় ধোঁয়াশা। কিন্তু এরই মাঝে সেপ্টেম্বরে আফগানিস্তানের বিপক্ষে সিরিজের সূচি চূড়ান্ত করে ফেলেছে ভারত। আনুষ্ঠানিক ঘোষণা না এলেও বাংলাদেশের বিপক্ষে ভারতের সিরিজটা যে আপাতত হচ্ছে না, তা এক প্রকার নিশ্চিতই বলা যায়। যে সময় বাংলাদেশের বিপক্ষে সিরিজ খেলার কথা ছিল, সেই সময়ে আফগানিস্তানের বিপক্ষে তিন ম্যাচের টি-টোয়েন্টি সিরিজ খেলবে ভারত। বিষয়টিকে বাংলাদেশ সিরিজ বাতিলের পরোক্ষ ইঙ্গিত হিসেবেই দেখছে ক্রীড়াভিত্তিক ওয়েবসাইট ক্রিকবাজ। পূর্বনির্ধারিত সূচি অনুযায়ী, তিনটি করে ওয়ানডে ও টি-টোয়েন্টি খেলতে আগামী ২৮ আগস্ট বাংলাদেশে আসার কথা ছিল ভারতের। ১ থেকে ১৩ সেপ্টেম্বরের মধ্যে এই দুই সিরিজের ম্যাচ অনুষ্ঠিত হওয়ার কথা ছিল। তবে আফগানিস্তানের বিপক্ষে ভারতের সিরিজের সূচি চূড়ান্ত হওয়ায় ফের অনিশ্চয়তায় পড়েছে বাংলাদেশ সফর। ফলে নির্ধারিত সময়েও সিরিজটি মাঠে গড়ানোর সম্ভাবনা কমে গেছে এবং ভারতের বাংলাদেশ সফর আরও এক দফা পিছিয়ে যাওয়ার পথেই রয়েছে। আগামী ১৩, ১৫ ও ১৭ সেপ্টেম্বর দিল্লির অরুণ জেটলি স্টেডিয়ামে মুখোমুখি হবে ভারত ও আফগানিস্তান। তিন ম্যাচের টি-টোয়েন্টি সিরিজের বিষয়টি নিশ্চিত করেছেন আফগানিস্তান ক্রিকেট বোর্ডের (এসিবি) প্রধান নির্বাহী নাসিব খান। #cricket #cricketnews #NewsUpdate #somoytv

An explosive-laden drone was steered toward parked Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport, according to German investigators. Perpetrators installed an antenna near the airport to amplify the control signals and direct the drone at the aircraft. Per the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA), the drone was controlled via the cellular network, enabling operation from anywhere in the world. It was fitted with a camera, a 5G router, two SIM cards, and an extra battery for a longer flight time. It lacked position lights. Next to their boardroom they need a readtheroom.

VIDEO | Delhi: Speaking after the pre-screening of short film ‘Devyani’, Ashwani Kumar IAS Director, DITEC & Secretary IT, Government of Assam says, "In today's society, women and daughters-in-law are often made to feel that nobody is happy when a girl is born into the family. People think it is a shock, that they will have to pay dowry for the girl, or that girls are bad or inauspicious. But that is not the whole picture. There are many people who want to have a daughter, but there is a fear in their minds because of the situation in society. When a girl goes out, there is always uncertainty about whether she will return safely. She may face harassment every day, outside and even from her own relatives and at home. There is a mindset where everyone wants to protect themselves from that crisis. People worry about how they will ensure their daughter's safety if they have one, and this concern continues to trouble them. This is not about the financial aspect; it is a different kind of problem that I have seen and experienced, and that is what I have tried to portray in this film." We discussed the need to accelerate the procurement, with JICA’s @JICA_direct_en support, of 62 power transformers for frontline regions. Together with our Japanese partners, we are also working on procuring specialised equipment for gas production. We are equally interested in exploring opportunities for cooperation on the restoration and modernisation of Ukraine’s thermal power plants (TPPs) and combined heat and power plants (CHPs) during 2027-2030. We deeply value Japan’s support and our partners’ readiness to continue our cooperation in strengthening Ukraine’s energy resilience. اوکراین و روسیه در طول شب گذشته (۱۰- اا اگست) به حملات متقابل خود ادامه دادند و ولادمیر زیلینسکی رییس جمهور اوکراین ، مسکو را به استفاده از میزایل های بالیستیک کوریای شمالی متهم کرد. رییس‌جمهور اوکراین گفت در حملات روز سه شنبه روسیه به زاپوریژیا که دست‌کم شش کشته و حدود ۱۹ زخمی بر جای گذاشت، از میزایل های بالستیک کوریای شمالی نیز استفاده شده است. او کراین نیز درحملات متقابل ، گدام های متعلق به فروشگاه اینترنتی وایلدبیریز را در جنوب روسیه هدف قرار داد. این شرکت که به "امازون روسیه" معروف است، در هفته‌های اخیر بارها هدف حمله قرار گرفته است. این حملات یک روز پس از آن انجام شد که دست‌کم ۱۳ نفر، از جمله یک کودک، در حملات طیارات بی سرنشین اوکراین به جمهوری تاتارستان روسیه، در فاصله بیش از ۱۱۰۰ کیلومتری از مرز اوکراین، کشته شدند. کنسولگری ازبکستان در تاتارستان اعلام کرد که هفت نفر از کشته‌شدگان شهروند ازبکستان بودند. زیلینسکی در سخنرانی ویدیویی شام روز دوشنبه گفت : " روسیه برای اولین بار نمی‌تواند بدون نیروهای کمکی کوریای شمالی به جنگ ادامه دهد". وی افزود "هرچه حملات کوریای شمالی در اینجا در اوکراین و در اروپا بیشتر باشد، هرچه راکت ها و سربازان آنها بیشتر مورد استفاده قرار گیرند، آنها بیشتر کاستی‌ها و نقاط کور خود را اصلاح می‌کنند". زیلنسکی افزود که این مسئله برای سایر نقاط جهان نیز خطر ایجاد می‌کند. زیلنسکی این نگرانی را در حال ابراز میکند که اوکراین با کمبود شدید راکت های رهگیر پتریوت روبه‌رو است. اوکراین در حالی که خود را برای تشدید حملات میزایل های بالستیک روسیه در زمستان پیش‌رو آماده می‌کند، به‌گونه فوری به دنبال صدها راکت رهگیر دافع هوای پتریوت است. کییف در ماه جولای تنها ۲۹ فروند از ۱۹۵ میزایل بالستیک روسیه را رهگیری کرد؛ آماری که نشان‌دهنده شکاف رو‌به‌رشد در توانایی‌های دفاع هوایی این کشور است. گرچه کشورهای اروپایی سیستم‌ها و راکتهای پتریوت را در اختیار اوکراین قرار داده‌اند، اما ذخایر خودشان نیز محدود است. ایالات متحده نیز با کاهش ذخایر میزایل روبه‌رو Reports of unidentified drones over Diego Garcia are raising new questions about the vulnerability of one of the U.S. military’s most strategically important—and remote—installations. The U.K. Ministry of Defence confirmed it was aware of the reported sightings but provided no details. U.S. Pacific Command (PACOM) likewise declined to discuss the incident or force-protection measures. The reports originated with an unofficial Air Force social media account, which claimed drones had been spotted near the base’s fuel farm and that a 0700–1900 curfew had been imposed. TWZ says it has not independently verified those claims. The timing is significant. Diego Garcia was already considered a priority target for Iran, with F-16s deployed to the island in February specifically for protection against one way attack drones and cruise missiles. Iran subsequently launched two ballistic missiles at the installation during Operation Epic Fury, though neither hit the base. The reported drone sightings highlight a different threat: long range or sea launched drones that could reach isolated bases far from conventional launch points. Diego Garcia sits roughly 1,000 miles from Sri Lanka and has virtually no civilian population that could plausibly account for recreational drone activity. In the past, Diego Garcia has been a temporary home for strategic U.S. bombers and has been used to reload U.S. Navy Arleigh Burke calss guided missile destroyer vertical launch system (VLS) cells with munitions like the SM-6 and Tomahawk.

Paikmal Aspirational Block in Bargarh district, Odisha, is promoting local craftsmanship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities under the Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP). Through the identification and mentoring of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and local artisans, the initiative is strengthening skills, improving product design, enabling value addition, and creating stronger market linkages. These efforts are helping artisans build resilient enterprises while preserving Odisha’s rich cultural traditions. A major milestone was the successful showcase of locally crafted bamboo products, terracotta, brassware, and herbal products at the renowned Bargarh Dhanu Yatra and other exhibitions, providing artisans with wider market access, greater visibility, and new opportunities to connect directly with consumers. By promoting innovation, strengthening women-led enterprises, and celebrating indigenous crafts, the Aspirational Blocks Programme is supporting sustainable livelihoods, preserving cultural heritage, and advancing inclusive rural development. #AspirationalBlocksProgramme #VocalForLocal @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

A new interview with Artem Kariakin, also known as Skhidnyi (@samotniyskhid), on the fighting in Kostiantynivka, the growing brutality of the war, and mobilization in Russia. I put together a brief summary of the key points: • Ukrainian troops are still present in Kostiantynivka, but that fact alone does not mean that the Armed Forces of Ukraine control the city. It would be more accurate to say that Ukrainian forces are trying to prevent the Russians from breaking out beyond Kostiantynivka. The situation there is extremely dynamic. Tomorrow, 15 troops may enter the area, and the day after tomorrow, hypothetically, there may already be 100, Skhidnyi explains. • With every attack, the Russians advance gradually, grinding down wave after wave of their assault troops, trading them for 100 meters in one place and another 100 meters somewhere else. For the past two years, essentially the same scenario has been playing out with almost no change. • Russian tactics and strategy remain largely unchanged: glide bombs, cutting logistics, the use of every available type of drone, and infiltration by small groups. District by district, meter by meter. • As long as a city has not yet been more or less burned to the ground, it can still be defended. But given the intensity of the bombardment and the number of glide bombs the Russians are dropping, after a certain point that becomes simply unrealistic. Under current conditions, when everything is being torn apart by glide bombs and logistics are being destroyed from the air, preparing a defense is extremely difficult. • Skhidnyi says that the cities beyond Kostiantynivka will be defended to the very end. In his view, the intensity, brutality, and ferocity of those battles will surpass every battle fought in the Donbas during this war. • Skhidnyi and his comrades are already seeing that the Russians are in a hurry and preparing for a final push to seize full control of the Druzhkivka–Kramatorsk–Sloviansk urban agglomeration. And they will be ground down in massive numbers in those assaults. • There is no doubt that an offensive toward Sloviansk and Kramatorsk is currently the Russian command’s absolute priority. Skhidnyi notes that the Russians do not have much time left before winter, which is forcing them to hurry, since offensive operations will become more difficult once winter sets in. • The Russians are trying to break into Mykolaivka in small groups. So far without success — Ukrainian forces are holding the defense there. In the Lyman area, Ukrainian troops are probably carrying out some of their most successful counterattacks. They have even managed to push Russian forces back. Russian troops are still far from capturing Lyman. • Skhidnyi stresses that the war is not merely becoming more brutal — it is going completely off the rails. Both Russians and Ukrainians, he says, are now entering a stage of mutual destruction of virtually everything. Anyone who thought the war was heading toward an end or even a pause is deeply mistaken. Skhidnyi says that, in his view, the worst is only beginning. • Speaking about casualty ratios, he says that on the hottest sectors of the front, where Russian forces are attacking most intensively, the ratio may reach 1 to 10 or even 1 to 15. Skhidnyi emphasizes that the Russians understand perfectly well what is happening — they simply do not care. • If Moscow decides to launch a new wave of mobilization in the fall, the situation for Ukrainian troops will become not merely difficult, but catastrophically difficult. Skhidnyi believes that large-scale mobilization could be carried out for only one purpose: to launch offensives on new sectors of the front, including in the north and potentially to increase pressure on Kyiv. • Skhidnyi gives a positive assessment of the Kursk operation, in which he personally took an active part, and says that without it, today’s front line would have taken shape a year earlier. The Kursk operation drew away Russian manpower as well as some of their best drone operator crews. • His comrades who were fighting in the Donbas at the time fully agree with that assessment: once Ukrainian forces crossed the Russian border, the pressure in eastern Ukraine eased considerably. Ukrainian forces were able to catch their breath and launch counterattacks. vot-tak.tv/94783734/boyec-vs…

Using Labour Force Survey data from 2001–02 to 2024–25 across 12 waves, the study applies an Age-Period-Cohort (APC) model to explore unemployment trends. Findings show that overall education do reduces unemployment , but younger, educated cohorts face significantly higher joblessness than older cohorts, particularly the ones with tertiary education. The results point to a growing graduate oversupply, skills mismatch, and a stagnant labor market demand, highlighting the need to better align education with labor market dynamics. নির্বাচন কমিশন (ইসি) সচিব আখতার আহমেদ বলেছেন, সংসদের অধিবেশন কক্ষে অনুষ্ঠিত হবে রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচনে ভোট গ্রহণ। আর ৩৪৯ সংসদ সদস্যের ভোট শেষে তাৎক্ষণিকভাবেই ফলাফল জানানো হবে। মঙ্গলবার (১১ আগস্ট) রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচন নিয়ে জাতীয় সংসদে বৈঠকে শেষে নির্বাচন কমিশনে সাংবাদিকদের তিনি এসব তথ্য জানান। প্রায় দুই ঘণ্টার বৈঠকের বিষয়ে নির্বাচন কমিশনে ব্রিফিংয়ে কমিশন সচিব আখতার আহমেদ বলেন, রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচনে ৩৪৯ জন ভোট দেয়ার সুযোগ পাবেন। ভোটগ্রহণ সরাসরি সম্প্রচার করা হবে। আর ২০ আগস্ট দুপুর ২টা থেকে বিকেল ৫টা পর্যন্ত রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচনের ভোটগ্রহণ চলবে। এর আগে সংসদ ভবনে রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচন নিয়ে সরকারি ও বিরোধী দলের সংসদীয় প্রতিনিধিদের সঙ্গে নির্বাচন কমিশন ও সংসদ সচিবালয়ের কর্মকর্তাদের বৈঠক হয়। ওই বৈঠক শেষে জাতীয় সংসদের সরকারি দলের চিফ হুইপ মো. নূরুল ইসলাম মণি বলেন, রাষ্ট্রপতি নির্বাচনে দলের সিদ্ধান্তের বাইরে কেউ ভোট দিতে পারবেন না। #NewsUpdate #news #nationalnews #somoytv

More Than a Platform: How WEP Built an Ecosystem Playbook for India’s Women Entrepreneurs The Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP), NITI Aayog, launched More Than a Platform: How WEP Built an Ecosystem Playbook for India’s Women Entrepreneurs, edited by Ms. Anna Roy, Mission Director, WEP. The book captures WEP’s journey in building a collaborative ecosystem to support women entrepreneurs through access to markets, finance, skilling, mentorship, business development services, and compliance and legal support. The launch brought together policymakers, women entrepreneurs, and ecosystem leaders. Shri Konda Vishweshwar Reddy, Member of Parliament from Chevella, Telangana, delivered a special address. Ms. Mira Kulkarni, Founder, Forest Essentials; Ms. Mita Gutgutia, Co-founder, Ferns & Petals; Ms. Gagandeep Bhullar, Founder & CEO, SuperHumanRace; and representatives from the Mann Deshi Foundation shared their perspectives and experiences on entrepreneurship, enterprise-building, and impact. The book was launched on 10 August 2026 at Rang Bhawan, New Delhi, marking an important milestone in WEP’s journey and in India’s efforts to strengthen the women entrepreneurship ecosystem. #WEP #MoreThanAPlatform @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 chaired a meeting to review preparations for the 14th South Asian Games, which Pakistan will host in March 2027. DPM/FM directed the establishment of subcommittees tasked with overseeing key aspects of the Games, including financing, infrastructure development and upgradation, athletes’ training and preparation, and logistical arrangements. He stressed the importance of timely planning and close coordination among all stakeholders to ensure that Pakistan hosts the Games to the highest standards. He emphasized that the 14th South Asian Games provide Pakistan with an important opportunity to showcase its sporting talent, hospitality and organizational capacity, while conveying to the world a message of peace, friendship, goodwill and harmony. The meeting was attended by SAPM Tariq Bajwa, President of the Pakistan Olympic Association Mr. Arif Saeed, Secretary IPC, Director General Pakistan Sports Board, officials of the Ministry of Finance, and representatives of the Governments of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

In view of the increasing frequency and intensity of incidents of cloudbursts, flash floods, landslides and extreme rainfall in Himachal Pradesh, a Multi-Sectoral Central Team (MSCT) has been constituted. The Team comprises experts from the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Central Building Research Institute (CBRI), Roorkee, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Indore, and other concerned agencies. In addition, inputs received from the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC) and Geological Survey of India (GSI) have also been incorporated.The Team has been entrusted with the responsibility of undertaking a scientific assessment of the causes of increasing extreme weather events in the State, analysing the geographical and ground conditions of the worst-affected areas, compiling and examining data received from various agencies, and recommending long-term measures to minimise the impact of such disasters. Assessments provided by weather experts, scientific institutions and State authorities indicate that, as a consequence of climate change, the intensity and frequency of extreme rainfall events are increasing in the Himalayan region. Accelerated snowmelt and moraine instability contribute to off-season slope failures and high runoff in high-altitude zones. As per MSCT study, anthropogenic factors have also contributed to the increased risk in the region.: MoS Home Nityanand Rai

The Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu has geographical area of 603 square km and population of 5,86,956 as per Census 2011. The Union Territory has adequate democratic mechanism to ensure participatory governance. The Union Territory is represented in the Lok Sabha through 02 elected Members of Parliament. In accordance with the provisions of 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment, the Union Territory has two-tier panchayat system in rural areas and municipal councils in urban areas. The elected local bodies, constituted under the "The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayat Regulation, 2012" play a significant role in local governance, development planning and implementation of welfare and developmental programmes. The Sarpanches of Gram Panchayats have been vested with adequate financial powers under "The Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Panchayats (Application of Funds and Maintenance of Accounts) Rules - 2024". No such proposal is under consideration of the Ministry at present.: MoS Home Nityanand Rai

Prof. K.V. Raju, Member, NITI Aayog, along with officials from NITI Aayog, visited Telangana from 05–07 August 2026 to engage with the State Government on key development priorities. During the visit, Prof. Raju held discussions with the Chief Secretary and senior officials of the State Government. He emphasised the need for adopting a uniform methodology for estimating District Domestic Product (DDP) and Primary Sector GDP to enable consistent assessment and support evidence-based decision-making at the district level. Detailed deliberations were also held on advancing the State’s implementation strategy for achieving the objectives outlined in the Vision Document and establishing an institutional mechanism for regular review of progress and resolution of implementation challenges. Prof. Raju also visited sites showcasing some of Telangana’s best practices, including initiatives under the National Mission on Edible Oils – Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), innovative horticulture farming practices, and the development of Genome Valley as a leading biotechnology and life sciences hub in India. The visit further strengthened the partnership between NITI Aayog and the Government of Telangana and reaffirmed the shared commitment to translating the State’s development priorities into a strategic roadmap towards the goals of Viksit Bharat by 2047. #Telangana #CooperativeFederalism @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

As artificial intelligence reshapes the global economy, the debate is moving beyond technology to questions of economic power, strategic capability, and national resilience. In an article published in Mint, Mr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser to the Government of India, and Ms. Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, argue that AI sovereignty should not be understood as complete self-sufficiency or technological isolation. Instead, the focus should be on identifying critical dependencies, building trusted partnerships, and developing the capabilities that matter most for long-term competitiveness. The article highlights the importance of strengthening domestic strengths in areas such as talent, manufacturing, data, compute, and innovation, while remaining deeply connected to global markets and value chains. It also underlines the need for selective strategic autonomy, where countries retain the ability to make independent choices in technologies that are essential for economic security and future growth. For India, the challenge is not to replicate every layer of the AI stack, but to build the capacity, institutions, and partnerships required to become a significant producer of technology, not merely a consumer of it. #ArtificialIntelligence #EconomicGrowth @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp @debjani_ghosh_

Eleven months after 26/11, the Congress-NCP government in Maharashtra was re-elected for a third term. The usual explanations are a divided opposition and Raj Thackeray's MNS splitting the Marathi vote. But before any of that, in February 2008, the state's electoral map was redrawn for the first time since 1976. Maharashtra's 2001 population divided by 288 seats gives about 3,36,000 people per constituency. Any tehsil smaller than that fits inside one seat, and the law says to keep administrative boundaries intact where you can. The order divided 85 tehsils. Check each against the 2011 census, three years later, when populations had only grown — 46 of those divisions were not needed on population grounds at all. In five districts, no tehsil was large enough to require cutting. But the delimitation order cut them anyway. Buldhana four times. In Bhandara, Gadchiroli and Sindhudurg it cut nothing. Then, look at the specifics. - Five wards of Aurangabad city, 69,535 people, were lifted out of the Aurangabad Lok Sabha seat and placed in Jalna. The government parties went on to win one of Aurangabad's six assembly segments, and five of Jalna's six. - Scheduled Castes were 17.1 per cent of that city and 28.6 per cent of those five wards. Outside the Mumbai and Pune belt, Aurangabad is the only city the order split between two parliamentary seats. It was the Shiv Sena's Marathwada stronghold. - RR Patil, the Home Minister, had won Tasgaon by 6,304 votes in 2004. The order added a whole neighbouring tehsil. In 2009 he won by 65,173, the largest improvement of any member in the state. - Ashok Chavan became Chief Minister in December 2008. The order had rebuilt Bhokar, a seat the NCP held by 6,702 votes, into three whole tehsils containing the ground Chavan had represented since 1999. He contested it in 2009 and won 79.65 per cent, the highest share in Maharashtra. - Nine of the state's ten safest seats went to the Congress or NCP. - Across Marathwada, the BJP and Shiv Sena fell from 25 seats of 45 to 9 of 46. The argument is not against redrawing the electoral map. Maharashtra's map remained untouched for 32 years before 2008 and has been untouched for 18 since. The longer a correction waits, the bigger it has to be, and the more can be buried inside it. A redraw that moves everything is the one that cannot be audited. The same is true for the national map also — Lok Sabha has been frozen at 543 seats on the 1971 census, when India had 55 crore people and a seat meant about 10 lakh. It now has 140 crore and a seat means 26 lakh. @deepeshgulgulia on 'Why India Should Redraw Its Electoral Map More Often, Not Less' — illustrated with relevant maps and infographics. swarajyamag.com/politics/why…

Ahmed Ali Fayyaz (@ahmedalifayyaz) ZERO PROGRESS ON DISTRICT HOSPITAL BUDGAM IN LAST 8 MONTHS This is the outcome of our struggle for 17 long years. Believe it or not, Budgam perhaps continues to be the country's only District without a District Hospital. A dispensary-type facility on 2 or 3 kanals of land has been named as District Hospital since 1980s. Even after the residents of Rishipora handed over more than 70 kanal of land free of all compensation to the authorities in 2007, Chief Minister Ghulam Nabi Azad's commitment of a full-fledged District Hospital was never implemented by any of the successive Governments. Finally the funding was approved, tenders were floated and the execution started in the incumbent LG's period in 2022-23. However, all ongoing works have been stopped by the elected Government on District Hospital Rishipora Budgam and the adjoining Critical Care Hospital in December 2025. The concerned authorities say that the entire funds allocation has been exhausted and additional funds to the tune of ₹30-40 crore have been demanded from the Government's Finance Department which are awaited. With the two most brilliant IAS officers being posted as FC/Additional Chief Secretary Finance and Deputy Commissioner of Budgam, and @CM_JnK @OmarAbdullah himself being the Minister incharge Finance, people of the area are optimistic about a breakthrough, resumption and completion of the suspended works, procurement and installation of the entire machinery, appointment of the medical, paramedical and administrative staff and operationalisation of the District Hospital within the final deadline. Abdul Hakim Sharaee, Minister of Justice of the Islamic Emirate and head of the Commission for the Prevention of Land Grabbing, said at a meeting at the ministry that implementing the special court’s rulings on seized state-owned land is a religious and legal obligation of the commission. According to a statement from the ministry, Sharaee said that once a court rules that a piece of land belongs to the state, the commission is obligated to implement the ruling. He added that the work of both the commission and the court is based on documents, evidence and laws. Sharaee also stressed that identifying and reclaiming seized land is a legal matter, describing attempts to link the process to ethnicity, religion or language as “illogical.” #TOLOnews_English

Ritika Verma from ICRIER recently moderated Pillar 1- Battery Data, Traceability & Systems Safety, at the Phase 2 Convening of the Circular Battery Ecosystem (CBE) Standards Working Group on 6 August 2026, convened by @UL_Standards and Battery 360. The session brought diverse perspectives to a critical question on how can India build a reliable, interoperable and future-ready data ecosystem that allows batteries to be traced safely across their lifecycle? Discussions spanned: 🔹 Battery identification and digital battery passports 🔹 Data standards and interoperability 🔹 Remaining Useful Life (RUL) 🔹 Battery safety and lifecycle traceability 🔹 Data governance and cybersecurity The conversation also examined the relevance of international standards and frameworks, and how these could be adopted, adapted or further developed for the Indian context. A key takeaway: battery traceability is not a technology challenge alone, it is equally a standards, governance and ecosystem challenge. As India scales its EV and battery ecosystem, common approaches to identification, data exchange, safety and lifecycle information will be central to making circularity work in practice. #CircularEconomy #BatteryTraceability #BatteryPassport #DataGovernance #EVs

1/5: The recent protests over examination failures mean that the government now has a rare political mandate to bring substantial reforms in the entrance examination system. Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif's Message on National Minorities Day 11 August 2026. Pakistan commemorates National Minorities Day every year with a firm resolve to acknowledge the invaluable presence of minorities, their inclusion in the national mainstream, and their significant contributions to the national progress and prosperity. The minorities living in Pakistan are an integral part of our national fabric and reflect the true beauty of our diverse social and cultural landscape. On 11 August 1947, while addressing the historic inaugural session of the Constituent Assembly, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah unequivocally affirmed the rights of minorities in Pakistan: “You are free; you are free to go to your temples, you are free to go to your mosques or to any other place of worship in the State of Pakistan. You may belong to any religion or caste or creed—that has nothing to do with the business of the State.” These historic words of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah hold an enduring and unforgettable place in Pakistan’s social order, system of governance and religious ethos. This day also serves as a reaffirmation of Pakistan’s unwavering commitment to unity among different segments and communities of society, peaceful coexistence, mutual respect, and equal opportunities for progress for all. Pakistan is a diverse society where people belonging to different faiths, cultures, nationalities and traditions live together in harmony. From the Pakistan Movement and the creation of Pakistan to the present day, minority communities have played a pivotal role in the country’s progress and national development. They have rendered invaluable services in the economic, educational, social, cultural and political spheres. The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan guarantees the protection of the rights and interests of minority communities. These constitutional safeguards are further reinforced by an effective legal framework. The country’s laws contain effective provisions for the protection of places of worship of minorities, prohibition of discriminatory practices, and prevention of hate speech. The enactment of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 2025 to safeguard the rights of minorities is undoubtedly a significant national milestone. Under the aboce stated Act, the Ministry of Human Rights is taking the necessary steps for the establishment of an independent commission. The Commission will play its role in redressing grievances, overseeing constitutional and legal safeguards, making recommendations regarding government policies and legislation, monitoring matters relating to places of worship and employment quotas, and promoting equality and inclusion. To promote interfaith harmony and social cohesion, the Interfaith Harmony Policy 2025 has been introduced, aimed at protecting religious freedom, promoting interfaith dialogue, and ensuring equal opportunities without discrimination. The Government is also implementing the National Policy for Countering Violent Extremism 2024. The Ministry of Human Rights, in consultation with all relevant stakeholders, has also introduced the National Action Plan for Human Rights 2026, which includes specific measures for the protection and promotion of the rights of minority communities. The Government of Pakistan, in collaboration with the provincial governments, relevant institutions and civil society, reaffirms its collective resolve to continue making every possible effort to protect the rights of every citizen, particularly those belonging to minority communities, ensure equal opportunities, and advance towards the goal of a peaceful, tolerant and united society.

🇫🇷 The AASM 250 HAMMER shows how modern precision strike works. 🎯 Its laser-guided variant doesn’t “ride” a laser beam. A Semi-Active Laser seeker detects energy reflected from the illuminated target and guides the weapon toward it. On Rafale, the TALIOS pod can track and designate targets, while HAMMER combines terminal laser guidance with INS/GPS navigation. The real challenge isn’t making lasers or detectors—it’s integrating seeker + navigation + guidance + flight controls into one compact system able to survive extreme speed, vibration and G-loads. 🇮🇳 India already operates HAMMER. Now BEL and Safran’s 50:50 JV aims to manufacture it in India with up to 60% indigenisation. From importing precision weapons → building the capability at home. 🇮🇳

The Washington Post reports that an Iranian assassination threat prompted a secret presidential extraction from Turkey last month, with Trump secretly transferred from the legacy Air Force One to a C-32A while the White House publicly maintained that he was aboard Air Force One. Trump reportedly left the 747 via an airport catering truck and boarded the C-32A, which flew to Britain under the call sign “Reach 18.” The legacy Air Force One, carrying journalists and staff who believed Trump was aboard, served as a decoy and continued to Britain under the AF1 call sign. The immediate reason was a credible Iranian threat against Trump or his aircraft following renewed U.S. strikes on Iran. The new Qatari-provided 747-8 was reportedly a factor because it lacked some of the defensive countermeasures found on the legacy presidential aircraft. The particularly notable part is that the deception extended to some White House personnel and journalists, who were not told Trump had changed aircraft.

Steven Jacobs, visited the CARICOM Secretariat for talks with a team headed by Adviser, Social Development, Beverly Harry-Emmanuel. Programme Manager, Culture at the CARICOM Secretariat, Dr. Hilary Brown presented on the background and evolution of CARIFESTA, which formed the basis of discussions on elements of the Region’s roving multidisciplinary, mega festival. Its wide range of events; financial, administrative, logistical and marketing components; and opportunities for creative industry development were among the agenda items. The inaugural CARIFESTA was held in 1972 in Guyana, which also hosted the festival in 2008. CARIFESTA XV was last held in Barbados in 2025. The teams also discussed regional youth development following an overview by Programme Manager, Youth Development, Michele Small-Bartley.

ریچارد بنت، گزارشگر ویژه حقوق بشر سازمان ملل متحد در امور افغانستان، درباره کشته‌شدن افراد در جریان عملیات طالبان در کابل ابراز نگرانی کرده و خواستار تحقیقات فوری و بی‌طرفانه درباره این موضوع شده است. او شامگاه دوشنبه (۱۹ اسد) در پیامی در ایکس نوشته است که درباره گزارش‌های مربوط به کشته‌شدن افراد در جریان عملیات‌ امنیتی در کابل، از جمله کشته‌شدن چهار نفر بر اثر تیراندازی در روز دوشنبه و هفت نفر دیگر در حوزه هشتم امنیتی کابل در روزهای اخیر، نگرانی‌های جدی وجود دارد. بنت نوشته است: «تحقیقات فوری و بی‌طرفانه در این زمینه ضروری است. هرگونه استفاده از نیروی مرگبار باید مطابق با قوانین بین‌المللی حقوق بشر، از جمله اصول ضرورت و تناسب، صورت گیرد.» بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/258880

Kate Mansey, Assistant Editor of The Times reported on the crime in 2007 and was the first journalist to secure an interview with Raffaele Sollecito, Knox's then Italian boyfriend. Knox was convicted of the murder in 2009 along Sollecito. She was sentenced to 26 years in prison but her conviction was overturned in 2011. Two years after that, the acquittal was overturned and a retrial ordered, with an appeals court convicting Knox of murder for a second time. But in 2015, the Italian Supreme Court definitively acquitted her. Sollecito was also acquitted and Rudy Guede, an Ivorian student who had a record of burglaries, was found guilty and sentenced to serve 16 years. 68 years ago this August, the world’s first nuclear-powered submarine, USS Nautilus (SSN 571), made history. During the highly secret “Operation Sunshine,” Nautilus successfully conducted the first submerged transit under the North Pole. Nautilus submerged in the Barrow Strait on August 1st and traveled under the polar ice cap for 96 hours, covering 1,590 nautical miles before surfacing near Greenland. For this unprecedented feat, commanding officer Commander William R. Anderson and his crew were personally congratulated by President Dwight D. Eisenhower and awarded the Presidential Unit Citation. This historic voyage was made possible by the development of a nuclear propulsion plant under the leadership of Captain Hyman G. Rickover at the Naval Reactors Branch of the Atomic Energy Commission.
