Indigenous knowledge has immense value. The right investment can turn that value into jobs, stronger businesses and more resilient rural economies. I saw this first-hand last year in Michoacán, Mexico, when I visited Purépecha communities supported by @IFAD. For generations, communities there have sustainably managed their forests and passed down skills such as pine resin tapping. Targeted investment is now driving local processing of that resin into higher-value products, strengthening value chains and generating income while protecting the forests they depend on. The same principle is delivering results elsewhere. In Peru, investment is unlocking opportunities for Indigenous communities to commercialize medicinal plants. In Bolivia, it has strengthened traditional alpaca and llama production against climate shocks. This is an important lesson for development finance. We do not need to choose between preserving ancestral knowledge and creating economic opportunity. With the right financing, we can do both. More than 40% of IFAD’s loan portfolio contributes to initiatives targeting Indigenous Peoples. On Indigenous Peoples Day, we remain committed to investing with Indigenous Peoples as partners in building resilient and inclusive rural economies. With its strikes on Moscow, Ukraine is taking disruption to a new level. The success of a long-range strike is not measured by impact alone. Even an intercepted attack closes airspace, disrupts flights and logistics, and erodes the sense of security. Russia cannot protect everything. It has more targets than air defences. Hitting the target magnifies the effect, but disruption begins before destruction. Yes, Russia will continue firing ballistic missiles at Ukrainian cities. But Putin’s problem is that Ukrainian suffering will no longer compensate Russians for disruption at home. As that disruption spreads, Russians will increasingly blame Putin and his corrupt regime for breaking the central bargain underpinning his rule since 2022: war was supposed to be something Ukrainians suffer, not them. The choice is Putin’s: wind down the war to preserve control, or tighten control at home to keep the war going. I would love to be wrong, but everything we know about him suggests he will choose the latter.

شہباز شریف، نائب وزیراعظم و وزیر خارجہ محمد اسحاق ڈار اور چیف آف آرمی اسٹاف و چیف آف ڈیفنس فورسز فیلڈ مارشل سید عاصم منیر کو ان کی مدبرانہ اور دور اندیش قیادت، پاکستان کا عالمی تشخص بلند کرنے اور ملک کے قومی مفادات کے مؤثر دفاع پر خراج تحسین پیش کیا گیا۔ کابینہ ارکان نے پاکستان، سعودی عرب اور ترکیہ کے درمیان تاریخی مشترکہ دفاعی معاہدے پر دستخط کو بھی اہم سفارتی و دفاعی پیش رفت قرار دیا۔ قرارداد نے اس معاہدے کو امت مسلمہ کے مابین اتحاد و اتفاق کو مزید تقویت دینے کے لیے ایک اہم قدم قرار دیا۔ کابینہ نے نیشنل ہاؤسنگ پالیسی 2026ء اور اس پر عملدرآمد کےلئے ایکشن پلان کی منظوری دے دی۔ کابینہ کو بتایا گیا کہ نیشنل ہاؤسنگ پالیسی قومی و بین الاقوامی ماہرین پر مشتمل ورکنگ گروپ نے تیار کی، جبکہ اس کی تیاری کے دوران وفاقی وزارتوں، صوبائی حکومتوں اور ترقیاتی شراکت داروں سے بھی مشاورت کی گئی۔ کابینہ کو بتایا گیا کہ پالیسی کا بنیادی مقصد تمام شہریوں کے لیے پائیدار، محفوظ اور معیاری رہائش کی فراہمی ہے۔ کابینہ نے ہدایت کی کہ ہاؤسنگ منصوبوں میں زوننگ قوانین کی مکمل پابندی یقینی بنائی جائے اور زمین کے مؤثر استعمال کے لیے عمودی رہائش (Vertical Housing) کو ترجیح دی جائے۔ ساتھ ہی کابینہ نے ہدایت کی کہ انرجی ایفیشنسی کوڈز کو بھی نیشنل ہاؤسنگ پالیسی کا لازمی حصہ بنایا جائے تاکہ نئی تعمیرات توانائی کے مؤثر اور ماحول دوست تقاضوں سے ہم آہنگ ہوں۔ کابینہ کو وزیراعظم کے ’اپنا گھر‘ اسکیم کے تحت پیش رفت پر بھی بریفنگ دی گئی۔ کابینہ کو بتایا گیا کہ اپنے گھر کے خواہشمند درخواست گزاروں کو مختلف بینکوں کی جانب سے 220 ارب روپے کے قرضوں کی منظوری دی جا چکی ہے، جبکہ کامیاب درخواست گزاروں کو 32 ارب روپے سے زائد کی رقوم بھی جاری کی جا چکی ہیں۔ کابینہ نے بورڈ آف انویسٹمنٹ کی جانب سے پیش کی گئی سمری پر پاکستان اور سویڈن کے درمیان 1981ء میں طے پانے والے دو طرفہ سرمایہ کاری کے معاہدے کے خاتمے کا نوٹس واپس لینے کی منظوری دے دی۔ وزارت انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی کی جانب سے کابینہ کو پاکستان انفارمیشن سکیورٹی فریم ورک 2026ء (PISF 2026) کا مسودہ پیش کیا گیا۔ کابینہ کو بتایا گیا کہ یہ فریم ورک CERT Rules 2023ء کے تحت تیار کیا گیا ہے، جس کا مقصد انفارمیشن سکیورٹی کے بنیادی یکساں معیارات کا ایک جامع اور متحد نظام وضع کرنا اور مرکزی نگرانی کو یقینی بنانا ہے۔ کابینہ نے پاکستان انفارمیشن سکیورٹی فریم ورک 2026ء کی منظوری دیتے ہوئے اسے سائبر سکیورٹی کے لیے ایک اہم راہنما دستاویز قرار دیا اور ہدایت کی کہ اس پر مقررہ مدت کے اندر مؤثر انداز میں عملدرآمد یقینی بنایا جائے۔ وفاقی کابینہ نے 28 جولائی کو منعقدہ کابینہ کمیٹی برائے توانائی (CCoE) کے اجلاس میں لئے گئے فیصلے کی بھی توثیق کی۔ اس فیصلے کے تحت پاکستان آئل ریفایننگ پالیسی 2023 میں مجوزہ ترامیم کی توثیق کی گئی جن کے مطابق آئل ریفائنریز کی اپگریڈیشن کی جائے گی تاکہ ملکی توانائی کی ضروریات کو بہتر انداز میں پورا کیا جا سکے۔ کابینہ نے 27 جولائی اور 4 اگست کو منعقدہ اقتصادی رابطہ کمیٹی (ECC) کے اجلاسوں میں لئے گئے فیصلوں کی توثیق کی۔ اجلاس میں کابینہ کمیٹی برائے قانون سازی (CCLC) کے 24 جولائی کو منعقدہ اجلاس میں لیے گئے فیصلوں کی بھی توثیق کی گئی. Lahiri, Vice Chairperson, NITI Aayog, addressed the inaugural session of the Cheistha Kochhar Nudge Awards at India International Centre, New Delhi, reflecting on the role of behavioural economics in designing more effective and citizen-centric public policies. In his address, he highlighted that public policy must be designed around how people actually behave, taking into account biases, bounded rationality, and real-world decision-making constraints. He emphasised the importance of evidence-based nudges, field experiments, and digital public infrastructure in improving governance outcomes. Here is a small reminder for everyone spreading the pro-russian narrative about "revenge for Wildberries," as well as for any normal person who doesn't follow the war closely and feels confused. Pay attention to the dates! ​Russia struck the Amstor Shopping Mall in Kremenchuk on June 27, 2022, with cruise missiles in the middle of the day while up to 1,000 people were inside. 21 people died, and over 70 were injured. ​Russia struck the Epicentr Hypermarket in Kharkiv on May 25, 2024. It was a weekend afternoon, and around 200 civilians and staff were inside shopping for home supplies. The blast sparked a high-temperature chemical and building-material fire. We had to use DNA testing to identify victims. 19 were killed, including children, and 46 were injured. ​Russia struck the Kostiantynivka Central Market and surrounding shops at least twice: September 6, 2023, and August 9, 2024. Both strikes targeted dense retail zones crowded with shoppers during morning or early afternoon hours. 17 were killed and 32 injured in the September 2023 strike, and 14 were killed and 44 injured in the August 2024 strike on the Eko-Market. ​Russia struck the Nova Poshta Sorting Terminal in Korotych, Kharkiv region, on October 21, 2023. Late at night, while employees were unloading civilian mail, parcels, and humanitarian packages, two S-300 missiles hit a location where missiles arrive faster than they can be detected. The 8 people killed stood no chance, 15 people were injured. ​Russians continued to strike Nova Poshta in Korotych on January 13, 2026, killing 4 people and injuring 6; on July 19, 2026, killing 4 people and injuring 19; and on August 2, 2026, killing a driver. Among all the attacks listed, only the latest two occurred after the beginning of Ukrainian strikes on Wildberries. ​Russia struck the ATB Supermarket & Retail Square in Kherson on May 3, 2023. Hitting civilian shopping infrastructure during daytime hours, they trapped shoppers inside the burning grocery hall. 23 people were killed across Kherson that day: 4 inside the ATB supermarket, 1 inside the Epicentr store, and others at nearby transport stops and shops. ​Russia struck the Kherson Central City Market on October 1, 2024. Around 9:00 AM, artillery rounds landed directly in active outdoor market stalls. 7 were killed and 3 were injured. ​Finally, Russia struck Kramatorsk Central Station on April 8, 2022, during an active civilian evacuation. A Tochka-U ballistic missile hit packed evacuation platforms, killing 63 civilians, including 9 children, and injuring over 150. They also struck Chaplyne Railway Station on August 24, 2022, where an Iskander missile hit passenger trains and adjacent cars, killing 25 civilians and burning passenger carriages. ​This is a tiny fraction of Russian strikes on Ukrainian retail chains, markets, and civilian transportation infrastructure during the full-scale invasion. A tiny, little fraction! So when you brain-dead amoebas write "revenge for Wildberries," think again. Russia was bombing Ukraine all these years, long before our attacks on Wildberries, and they will continue regardless.

NUEVA POLÉMICA CON ROSALÍA: AGRADECIÓ A LA ARGENTINA TRAS SUS SHOWS Y DESATÓ UN RECLAMO INESPERADO Las palabras “Gracias, Argentina” resonaron en las redes sociales luego de que Rosalía culminara su serie de conciertos en el país y decidiera despedirse con un mensaje explícito de agradecimiento. La artista no solo expresó en letras mayúsculas su gratitud, sino que acompañó esas palabras con una galería de fotos que reflejaron diferentes momentos de su paso por Buenos Aires. Las imágenes, entre las que se destacan escenas del espectáculo, instantes de intimidad y detalles cotidianos, ofrecieron una crónica visual de su experiencia para los seguidores. La reacción de Rosalía tras sus conciertos en la Argentina se convirtió en motivo de conversación internacional, ya que el tono afectuoso del mensaje y la selección de imágenes contrastaron con la ausencia de saludos similares hacia otros países visitados durante la gira. Fanáticos de Chile y Colombia utilizaron las mismas plataformas para manifestar su descontento, reclamando un trato equitativo y preguntándose por qué la artista no había dedicado un post especial a sus públicos. I invited some friends to explore why these books resonate, how they can shape our understanding of ourselves and each other, and why literature matters now more than ever. I hope you’ll check it out starting September 24 on Audible and discover or rediscover books that stay with you long after you read them.

A while back, I revisited a few of the books that made an impact on me as a young man, influencing how I think about family, faith, race, politics and America: The Fire Next Time by James Baldwin, Song of Solomon by Toni Morrison, All the Pretty Horses by Cormac McCarthy, Gilead by Marilynne Robinson, All the King’s Men by Robert Penn Warren, and Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy by John le Carré.

At a time when fewer people are able to sit down with a book, it’s important to remember the joy and power that can come from reading. And some books don’t just tell a story – they change the way we see the world. That’s why I’m excited to share my latest podcast from @Audible_com and @HGMedia, A Great Book with Barack Obama.

PRESS RELEASE Family Expresses Gratitude To All Who Participated in Buhari’s Burial and Prayers The most senior member of the Buhari family, the family of the late President, Muhammadu Buhari, Malam Mamman Daura has, on behalf of the family expressed gratitude to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his wife, the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu for their role and that of Government of the Federation before, and after the passing of the former president. “It is truly comforting to receive such support from the President and the Vice President, Kashim Shettima, who went to the United Kingdom, and here in Daura, for the days he and the ministers during the mourning period. These have instilled confidence in all of us to face this loss with courage. “We are deeply grateful to the President on his thoughtful gestures in declaring a public holiday and renaming the University of Maiduguri after Buhari. “Our gratitude also goes to leaders of the various countries around the globe who either came in person, sent representatives, sent letters, or placed personal telephone calls to commiserate with us. Of special note were those of the King of England, King Charles III, the Secretary General of the United Nations, the Deputy Secretary General, Amina Mohammed, the Chairman of the African Union, and that of the Committee of Heads of State and Government of ECOWAS countries, and our former Head of State, Abdulsalami Abubakar. “Muhammadu Buhari’s demise is an irreparable loss and its pain is beyond words, but the general reaction and kind expressions give us the strength to cope with the loss of our esteemed family member and former leader of the country. “The family is equally grateful to Vice President Kashim Shettima in his own person and his wife, and to all state governors, especially those of Katsina, the host governor Dr Dikko Umar Radda; Professor Babagana Umara Zulum of Borno State and all those who visited us in the UK and Daura from Adamawa, Kano, Kwara, Lagos, Kaduna, Imo, Nasarawa, Bauchi, Sokoto, Kebbi as well as the several former governors, including Dr Peter Obi for their compassionate words of condolence. Your empathy has touched our hearts deeply, and we are truly grateful for your kindness. "We express our deep appreciations to former Vice Presidents Atiku Abubakar, Architect Namadi Sambo, Professor Yemi Osinbajo, and Ambassador Babagana Kingibe as well as to the President of Senate, Godswill Akpabio, the Speaker, House of Representatives, Honorable Tajuddeen Abbas, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin and the other leaders and members of the National and State Assemblies. “We do sincerely thank the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume and his predecessor in office, Boss Mustapha, the current Chief of Staff, Honorable Femi Gbajabiamila and his predecessor, Professor Ibrahim Gambari, former and serving members of the cabinet in both administrations for their activities in these events and their comforting words. “We are very pleased with the amazing gestures of our traditional leaders, notably the Sultan of Sokoto, the Shehu of Borno, the Emir of Gwandu and the host emirs of Katsina and Daura, as well as the various emirs and chiefs from all over Nigeria and the neighboring countries who came in person or sent representatives. “We have been honored by the large turnout of religious leaders, Islamic, Christian and of other faiths, community leaders, women, youth and politicians of various leanings whose surge in Daura was both challenging and reassuring. “The family in Daura is also thanking past and serving security and intelligence, police and military leaders, permanent secretaries, and the rank and file civil servants, community groups and associations, civil society, and the media of communications. 1/2

As Guyana 🇬🇾 prepares to host the 16th edition of the Caribbean Festival of Arts (CARIFESTA) in 2027, representatives of the #CARICOM Secretariat held discussions with the country’s Ministers who hold responsibility for culture. Minister of Culture, Youth and Sport, Hon. Charles S. Ramson, and Minister within that Ministry, Hon. Steven Jacobs, visited the CARICOM Secretariat for talks with a team headed by Adviser, Social Development, Beverly Harry-Emmanuel. Programme Manager, Culture at the CARICOM Secretariat, Dr. Hilary Brown presented on the background and evolution of CARIFESTA, which formed the basis of discussions on elements of the Region’s roving multidisciplinary, mega festival. Its wide range of events; financial, administrative, logistical and marketing components; and opportunities for creative industry development were among the agenda items. The inaugural CARIFESTA was held in 1972 in Guyana, which also hosted the festival in 2008. CARIFESTA XV was last held in Barbados in 2025. The teams also discussed regional youth development following an overview by Programme Manager, Youth Development, Michele Small-Bartley.

🇨🇴 ⚠️ A powerful earthquake has rocked Colombia and neighbouring Latin American countries, with at least 18 people confirmed dead in first reports as shocked residents surveyed destroyed buildings. Emergency teams rushed to help victims and search for survivors in the rubble after geologists recorded the quake at a magnitude of 7.4 with an epicenter 100 km (60 miles) deep in the west of the country. The early-morning quake was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela -- itself hit by a devastating quake in late June -- and prompted building evacuations in the Colombian capital Bogota, AFP reporters saw. News footage showed collapsed buildings across western Colombia, though officials said they did not fear a tsunami. At least 18 people were killed in the city of Pereira alone, Mayor Mauricio Salazar told Caracol Radio, adding "the situation is critical." 📷 Jonh Bonilla

Ambassador of Republic of Kazakhstan to Pakistan Yerzhan Kistafin called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on 10 August 2026.

ISLAMABAD: 10 August 2026. Upon completion of his tenure, H.E. Mr. Yerzhan Kistafin, Ambassador of the Republic of Kazakhstan to Pakistan, paid a farewell call on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House today. Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Sen.Mohammad Ishaq Dar, SAPM Tariq Fatemi and Foreign Secretary Amb. Amna Baloch were also present. The Prime Minister appreciated the Kazakh Ambassador's valuable contribution towards further strengthening the historic bonds of friendship and cooperation between Pakistan and Kazakhstan during his tenure. He especially acknowledged the Ambassador's role in facilitating the visit of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to Pakistan in February 2026, which elevated bilateral relations to the level of a Strategic Partnership. The Prime Minister conveyed his warm regards to President Tokayev and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to deepening the multifaceted partnership with Kazakhstan, including through enhanced regional connectivity, expanded trade linkages, and closer collaboration in the fields of energy, education, and people-to-people exchanges. Ambassador Kistafin thanked the Prime Minister for the cooperation and assistance extended to him during his tenure and expressed confidence that the trajectory of Pakistan-Kazakhstan relations would continue to grow under the strategic partnership framework. The Prime Minister wished the Kazakh Ambassador success in his future assignment. Video

Trump Gives Green Light to Saudi Nuclear Program The Donald Trump administration has finalized the draft of a bilateral nuclear agreement that authorizes Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium on its own territory. Although the negotiating teams have completed the terms, the document still awaits Trump’s final signature and approval by the U.S. Congress. This framework breaks with the region’s long-standing non-proliferation rules. Unlike the deal with the United Arab Emirates, which permanently renounced uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing while accepting strict IAEA inspections, the agreement with the Saudis does not require Riyadh to adopt the Agency’s inspection regime. Oversight will be limited to a bilateral pact between the United States and Saudi Arabia. This reinforces what Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has already said openly: if Iran gets a nuclear weapon, Saudi Arabia will want one too. It sounds like a clear signal that Riyadh believes Tehran already has, or is very close to having, the bomb, which explains the intense pressure they are putting on Washington. The situation puts the U.S. in a complicated position. Saudi Arabia’s ballistic missile program is developed in partnership with China, complete with technology transfers. If the Americans don’t give in now, the Saudis have plenty of money to look for other partners. This is not just about civilian nuclear energy. For that, it would be enough to buy reactors and import ready-made fuel. What Riyadh really wants is to master the full nuclear fuel cycle, especially domestic uranium enrichment. With this infrastructure, Saudi Arabia is building a nuclear latency capability: it will control the core technology needed to develop a weapon in relatively short order if pushed by an existential threat. Now that I’ve had a little time to reflect on DEF CON 34, I think what stays with me most isn’t actually standing on the stage. It’s the people. Of course, seeing a full house at Recon Village while talking about something I care deeply about - OSINT, critical thinking, and the cognitive consequences of relying too heavily on AI - was incredibly special. But walking around DEF CON afterwards and having people stop me just to say hello, tell me they enjoyed the talk, challenge an idea, or continue the conversation… That genuinely meant a lot to me. I got to reconnect with old friends and somehow leave Vegas with a whole bunch of new ones. And I got to spend several days surrounded by hackers, researchers, investigators, builders, curious minds and people who simply look at the world differently. That’s probably what I’ll remember most. I came to DEF CON to share some of my thoughts. I’m leaving having had my own thinking challenged and expanded in return. And perhaps that’s exactly what a gathering like DEF CON should do. So thank you DEF CON and Recon Village for having me. Thank you to everyone who came to the talk. And especially thank you to everyone who stopped me somewhere along the way just to talk, laugh, share an idea, grab a drink or say hello. I’m humbled, grateful, slightly exhausted, and leaving with far more ideas than I arrived with. DEF CON, you’ve been an absolute blast. I’ll be back. P.S. I will re-record my talk I gave at DEFCON and post this on my Github/Youtube. Please have a little patience with that. It will be online soon. #defcon34 #reconvillage #osint #ai @defcon @ReconVillage

NEW: Superb insider look at the shift within #Iran's top security council by @Alihashem: 🔹 The old line between Reformists and principlists no longer decides who holds power; new alliances are forming. Dismissal of Zolqadr as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council shows how quickly the ground is shifting. 🔹 Informed Iranian political source says Zolqadr is close to Qalibaf, the parliament speaker who has gained ever greater prominence by virtue of leading negotiations with the Trump administration. Notably, he is also father-in-law of deputy FM Gharibabadi—a familiar face in the negotiating sessions in Pakistan. There's also the detail that only a single member of the SNSC opposed the Iran-US MoU—and it was not Zolqadr. 🔹 So in the grander scheme of things, change at the SNSC looks like a balancing act by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, meant to check Qalibaf's rising influence. But at the same time, the hardline core of the security establishment is also tightening its grip around Iran’s new 56-year-old top decision maker, and vice versa. 🔹 Mohsen Rezaee's stock is rising for all these reasons. His longstanding seat inside the heart of Iran's national security establishment, his decades of experience in military, political and strategic affairs, and his roots in the Revolutionary Guards' hardline camp—all of these factors put him at the center of this moment in Iran’s history. 🔹 Even as Zolqadr was “forced out” per one senior Iranian political source, the net impact on Iran-US diplomacy is likely to be “good.” 🔹 According to multiple sources familiar with the selection process, Ali Baqeri-Kani—a former deputy foreign minister who is serving as the SNSC deputy secretary for international affairs—was the first name floated for the top position. But Pezeshkian, who heads the council in his capacity as president, is said to have turned down Baqeri-Kani. 🔹 Disagreement within the government over how to handle Zolqadr's exit held up the change, a delay that the president himself alluded to in an Aug. 8 interview. More appointments in Iran's military establishment are expected soon, expanding the picture that the new SNSC secretary is meant to complete. 🔹 As Iranian negotiators await the SNSC’s final input on negotiations with Oman over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, and by extension next steps on the MOU, Rezaee may face his first test in his new role sooner rather than later.

My prediction proved on the dot #Advertising Profit (@Profitpk) Television is dead. How do we know this? Because even your grandmother watches her dramas on YouTube. And the advertisers have noticed. Which is why 48% of Hum TV’s revenue from March 2025 to March 2026 came from YouTube. But that doesn’t mean Hum TV is making more money than before. Even though revenue from YouTube grew by 10% year-on-year, Hum TV’s overall revenue has actually gone down by 25% because traditional television advertising revenue fell by 40% in the same time period. That means advertisers are spending significantly less money on television ads, and more on social media because that is where the viewer has gone. And this is not just limited to Hum TV. Geo Entertainment and ARY, the other two major drama producers in Pakistan, are facing similar realities. Television is now going through what print went through years ago: the audience is shifting online and the advertisers are following the eyeballs. For Pakistan’s drama production industry, that means a significant change in the economics of television channels. If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

কুরিটিবার কৌতো পেরেইরা স্টেডিয়ামে কোরিটিবা ও শাপেকোয়েন্সের ম্যাচে ঘটে গেল অদ্ভুত এক ঘটনা। বক্সের ভেতর সুযোগ পেয়ে জ্যাসি মারানহাও বল জালে জড়ানোর পর দেরি না করে সতীর্থদের সঙ্গে উদযাপনে যোগ দেওয়ার বদলে ছুটে যান গ্যালারির দিকে, সমর্থকদের সঙ্গে আনন্দ ভাগ করে নিতে। বিজ্ঞাপনের বোর্ডের কাছে পৌঁছে মারানহাও গ্যালারির আরও কাছে যেতে সেটি টপকে যাওয়ার চেষ্টা করেন। কিন্তু বোর্ডের ওপাশে যে কোনো জায়গা নেই, বরং রয়েছে স্টেডিয়ামের টানেলের প্রবেশপথ— তা বুঝতে পারেননি তিনি। ফলে বোর্ড টপকানোর পরই ভারসাম্য হারিয়ে সোজা টানেলের ভেতরে পড়ে যান এই ব্রাজিলিয়ান ডিফেন্ডার। মুহূর্তের মধ্যেই ক্যামেরার ফ্রেম থেকে অদৃশ্য হয়ে যান মারানহাও। কয়েক সেকেন্ড ধরে মাঠের সবাই যেন হতবাক হয়ে তাকিয়ে ছিলেন, ঠিক কী ঘটেছে, সেটিই বোঝার চেষ্টা করছিলেন আশপাশের লোকজন। গোল উদযাপন করতে গিয়ে এমন অপ্রত্যাশিত দৃশ্য শেষ পর্যন্ত ম্যাচের অন্যতম আলোচিত মুহূর্তে পরিণত হয়। তবে কিছুক্ষণের মধ্যেই ঘটলো আরও মজার ঘটনা। মারানহাও যে গোলটি উদযাপন করতে গিয়ে টানেলের ভেতর পড়ে গেলেন, সেটি আদৌ বহাল থাকবে তো? উদযাপনের সেই মুহূর্ত পেরোতেই ম্যাচে হস্তক্ষেপ করে ভিএআর। গোলটি পুনরায় পর্যালোচনা করে রেফারি জানান, মারানহাও অফসাইড পজিশনে ছিলেন। ফলে গোলটি বাতিলের সিদ্ধান্ত আসে। যে গোল করে সমর্থকদের সঙ্গে উদযাপন করতে গিয়ে টানেলের ভেতর পড়ে গিয়েছিলেন ব্রাজিলিয়ান ডিফেন্ডার, শেষ পর্যন্ত সেই গোলের কোনো অস্তিত্বই থাকল না। গোল বাতিলের সিদ্ধান্তে ম্যাচের চিত্র বদলে গেলেও মারানহাওকে সামলাতে হয়েছে উদযাপনের সময় টানেলের ভেতর পড়ে যাওয়ার ধকলও। কোরিটিবা যখন ম্যাচের শেষ মুহূর্তগুলোতে জয় ধরে রাখার লড়াইয়ে ব্যস্ত, তখন ডান গোড়ালিতে বরফ বেঁধে বদলি খেলোয়াড়দের বেঞ্চে বসে ছিলেন এই ডিফেন্ডার। অবশ্য ম্যাচ শেষে নিজের শারীরিক অবস্থার বিষয়ে আশ্বস্ত করে মারানহাও জানান, তিনি ভালো আছেন। শেষ পর্যন্ত শাপেকোয়েন্সেকে ২-১ গোলে হারিয়ে জয় নিয়ে মাঠ ছাড়ে কোরিটিবা। তবে ম্যাচের ফলের চেয়েও মারানহাওয়ের সেই অদ্ভুত উদযাপনের দৃশ্যই দ্রুত ছড়িয়ে পড়ে সামাজিক যোগাযোগমাধ্যমে। #somoytv #NewsUpdate #sports

भारताची घोडदौड थांबवणे आता अशक्य मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या प्रमुख उपस्थितीत आज मुंबई येथे 'हर घर तिरंगा अभियान' अंतर्गत तिरंगा रॅली मोठ्या उत्साहात पार पडली. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, तिरंगा रॅलीच्या निमित्ताने आज या ठिकाणी महासागर पाहायला मिळत आहे. या तिरंग्याकरिता क्रांतिकारकांनी बलिदान दिले, सैनिकांनी सीमेवर मरण पत्करले, तमाम भारतवासियांनी संघर्ष केला, तो तिरंगा 15 ऑगस्ट 1947 ला मध्यरात्री फडकला आणि तो चंद्र आणि सूर्य आहेत तोपर्यंत डौलाने फडकत राहील. देशाचे पंतप्रधान नरेंद्र मोदी यांच्या नेतृत्वामध्ये भारत जगातली चौथी सर्वात मोठी आर्थिक महासत्ता बनलेला आहे. भारत सर्वच क्षेत्रात प्रगती करत आहे. जगातला कुठलाच देश चंद्राच्या दक्षिण ध्रुवावर आपलं अंतरिक्ष यान उतरवू शकला नाही. पण हे कठीण कार्य भारताच्या वैज्ञानिकांनी साध्य करून दाखवले. तसेच अमेरिकेनंतर अंतराळामध्ये पहिल्यांदा खासगी कंपनीच्या माध्यमातून अंतराळ यान सोडणारा आपला देश आहे. जगातील दुसऱ्या क्रमांकाची सगळ्यात मोठी स्टार्टअप इकोसिस्टीम म्हणून भारत जगासमोर उभा राहिला असल्याचेही मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी This is where a likely policy intervention through dedicated PLI allocation can be crucial. In 2021, the government had announced Rs 24000 cr PLI support for high-efficiency Solar PV modules, which has been a success. Yes, I think that is one the most common misconceptions. Original, core China is the wheat & millet country. Rice cultivating lands are a later addition (It so happened that Westerners have mostly interacted with the Far South, and that shaped their perceptions of the country) Will (@Evolving_Moloch) I've complained about this before but I found the claims about African Americans being adapted to hunting and gathering on the savanna and East Asians having a 'culture of doing homework' due (at least in part) to the 'arduous demands of the rice paddy' really annoying for at least half a dozen reasons: 1) Hunting and gathering largely disappeared from West Africa thousands of years ago. 1a) The notion that populations are narrowly adapted to a single subsistence system is nonsense in my view, but even if you accept that as the case then based on the long ubiquity of agriculture in West Africa African Americans would be adapted to farming not hunting and gathering. 1b) Most African American ancestry comes from groups that inhabited forests, not the savanna. But millet and sorghum are grown in savannas anyway, so the claim is wrong in multiple directions. 1c) While not strictly the same as Asian rice paddies, West Africa is one of two regions where rice was independently domesticated and intensive wet rice cultivation has a long history there. 2) Rice paddy cultivation spread through many unrelated language families, including with the Austronesian expansion. 2a) If you take those IQ estimates at face value then most populations reliant on rice paddy cultivation have lower IQs than African Americans, in the high 70s or low 80s. 2b) In relation to 1), rice paddy cultivation reached places like Korea and Japan after farming was already ubiquitous in West Africa. 2c) The original 'homework culture', the imperial exam system in China, emerged in the north in regions reliant on wheat not rice. And as noted in this thread below if you accept the results from the latest ancient DNA papers from the Reich lab and elsewhere there's no evidence for anything special selection wise about rice paddies, and most of the high performing East Asian population structure which the hereditarian perspective emphasizes comes from millet farmers. One point I will add in fairness, if it needs to be said: obviously the Arday thing is deeply revealing and embarrassing for Cambridge and I thought Cofnas' article exposing that was good. It's not a topic I focus on really but since that is relevant context for why Cofnas' views are currently being discussed I figure I should acknowledge that, because I don't want to, like, pile on criticism in a culture war sense that appears to distract or discredit a genuine contribution. PHOTO | Delhi: IT Minister, Delhi, Pankaj Kumar Singh introduced the ‘Delhi (Right of Citizens to Time Bound and Ease of Delivery of Services) Bill, 2026’ in the Delhi Legislative Assembly during the ongoing Monsoon Session. The proposed legislation aims to ensure that citizens of Delhi receive government services within stipulated timelines, in a transparent manner and without unnecessary visits to government offices. The Bill will replace the existing legislation enacted in 2011. The new provisions will fix accountability for officials who delay service delivery without valid reasons or reject applications improperly. A penalty of Rs 250 per day, up to a maximum of Rs 5,000, may be imposed on the concerned official. (Full video available on PTI Videos - ptivideos.com)

QUÉ FACTORES SON DETERMINANTES PARA LAS EMPRESAS A LA HORA DE CONTRATAR PERSONAL Y DEFINIR SALARIOS La discusión salarial en la Argentina atraviesa una etapa distinta a la de los últimos años. Durante el período de inflación muy alta, las paritarias giraban casi exclusivamente en torno a un objetivo: evitar que el salario perdiera demasiado poder adquisitivo. Hoy, la negociación salarial y las decisiones de contratación combinan variables que antes quedaban en un segundo plano, como la rentabilidad de cada empresa, el costo laboral, la productividad y la evolución del consumo. En ese marco, la inflación sigue siendo la referencia central, pero ya no es la única. “Hoy empiezan a pesar más la situación particular de cada empresa, su rentabilidad, la evolución de las ventas, el costo laboral y los salarios que paga el mercado”, explicó Paula Pía Ariet, economista especializada en Recursos Humanos y CEO de Gestión Capital Humano. 3/3 🇮🇳 MODI DIDN’T JUST INHERIT A FIGHTER SHORTAGE. INDIA STARTED CHANGING THE EQUATION. Instead of measuring air power only by squadron numbers, the focus expanded toward an indigenous, layered combat ecosystem. ✈️ Make in India: Tejas Mk1A → Mk2 → AMCA 🚀 Longer reach: BrahMos, Astra & Rudram families 🛡️ Layered air defence: S-400 + indigenous Akash/next-gen systems 📡 Sensors & networks: AEW&C, radars, data-linked warfare 🤖 Unmanned warfare: Ghatak, CATS Warrior & swarms 🇮🇳 Indigenisation: radars, EW, weapons, avionics & eventually engines Meanwhile, the projected fighter roadmap itself could deliver 896–1,166 aircraft through ~2050. So the comeback isn’t simply: 30 squadrons → 42 squadrons. It is a shift from dependence on imported platforms toward an increasingly Indian fighter + missile + drone + sensor + layered air-defence kill web. The squadron deficit became the catalyst for building a far deeper indigenous air-power ecosystem. 🇮🇳🔥

2/3 🚨 THIS IS WHERE CONGRESS MUST ANSWER. The UPA knew legacy fighters were ageing. It knew squadrons would retire. And it knew fighter procurement takes years. Yet: 2007: 126-fighter MMRCA process launched 2012: Rafale selected as L1 2014: UPA leaves office Result: ZERO MMRCA fighters contracted. The retirement curve wasn’t a surprise. Every year lost meant ageing aircraft moved closer to retirement while replacements moved further into the future. The question is simple: If they knew the squadron crunch was coming, where was the urgency?

1/3 🇮🇳 IAF FIGHTER SQUADRONS: THE ROAD BACK TO 42 India once operated around 41–42 fighter squadrons. Then came a long decline as ageing fleets retired faster than replacements arrived. 🔺 1990s: ~41–42 🔻 Late 2020s: ~29–31 🔵 2030–35: ~35–36 🟢 2040s: pathway toward 40–42 MiG-21s, MiG-23s and MiG-27s disappeared. Jaguars, MiG-29s and Mirages followed them toward retirement. The requirement was predictable. So how was the replacement pipeline allowed to fall so far behind? 🧵👇

Short update on the Dobropillia/Ocheretyne direction. The situation has become more difficult, and open source maps are behind on the extent of Russian advances and infiltration. This is true both to the east and south of the city as part of the Center Group of Forces' plan to encircle the city from both directions. Russia's rate of advance towards Dobropillia and Druzhkivka has increased in recent weeks. Small Russian infiltration groups from the 177th Naval Infantry Regiment have reached the southeastern part of Dobropillia, and other groups have made it north and northeast of Hannivka on the T0514 road moving from Novyi Donbas. Russia's 9th Motorized Rifle Brigade and 61st Naval Infantry Brigade are attempting to encircle Dobropillia from from the east/northeast using the high ground (including a height south of Stepy), while the 177th is approaching Dobropillia from the east along the T0515 road. Russian forces have reached the mine east of Chernihivka, which will serve as a hub for UAV crews (terricons provide valuable high ground for antenna) and infiltration groups. Russian presence in Bilytske (from the 5th Motorized Rifle Brigade), Chernihivka, and Matyasheve is increasing. To the east, Russia has advanced in Kucheriv Yar and Torske, placing its forces less than 9km from Druzhkivka. This is in part due to the reinforcement of this direction with the 90th Tank Division's 228th and 239th regiments (they took part in the July 22nd mechanized assault), which indicates it is a priority. Further Russian advances in this direction will pose a greater threat to Druzhkiva from the south/southwest, and Dobropillia from the east/northeast. Taking more high ground will also enable Russia to threaten Ukrainian logistics in both directions. In particular, Russian forces could put the Oleksandrivka-Kramatorsk portion of the T0510 road under fire control, which would complicate Ukrainian logistics. Russian forces are employing 15 inch fiber optic cable FPVs in this direction with a range of 50km with strikes in Novodonetske. Novodonetske and Oleksandrivka are being regularly targeted by 1-2 Geran drones per day (5-10 on Dobropillia) and both are also targeted by glide bombs. Although Ukraine's middle strike campaign has raised the costs for Russia and complicated their logistics, Russia still has rough parity in FPVs in this direction and continues to receive sufficient artillery ammunition (the greater problem is the diversity of ammunition sources). The situation east of Kramatorsk and Slovyansk is also becoming more difficult (Russia's Southern Group of Forces was responsible for approximately half of Russia's gains in July), which will force Ukraine into a difficult choice where to commit reinforcements. At this rate, the battle for Dobropillia could begin in the coming weeks or months.

I believe that this war would have ended a year or two if the Ukrainians didn’t have drones because the Ukrainians have a significant shortage of manpower, a significant shortage of artillery. And in a war that was heavily dependent on just manpower and artillery, I think the Ukrainians would have collapsed a while ago. But the drones have really helped keep them in the fight in an important way. So that’s one dimension to the drone issue. Then there’s the whole question of using drones in long-range attacks into Mother Russia. And this of course is what the Ukrainians have been doing big time in recent months. And I don’t think that those attacks have had any meaningful impact on the course of the war. And of course as you were alluding to, if anything it speeded up the end of the war because there is good reason to think that the Russian response to these long-range drone attacks by the Ukrainians is that the Russians have decided to retaliate by attacking Odessa and other Ukrainian sites on the Black Sea. And this has had a devastating effect on Ukraine because so much of Ukraine’s agricultural product as well as its industrial product moves out of Ukraine via the Black Sea ports. And of course the most prominent one is Odessa. But what’s happened here, and it’s very important to emphasise this, is that the Russians have basically closed the Odessa ports. And the end result is that today Ukraine is effectively a landlocked country. And given the percentage of exports, Ukrainian exports that go out of those ports through the Black Sea, this is going to have devastating effects on the Ukrainian economy. Another useful interview with Deputy Chief of Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence Major General Vadym Skibitskyi. Some highlights: -Russia increased ballistic missile production by suspending production of Kinzhal and Kh-32, both of which have accuracy problems (greater than 30 meter deviation). -"Another example is Russia’s planned production of strike drones for August this year – Geran-1, Geran-2, Geran-3, Geran-4, Geran-5, Garpiya, Gerbera, Gerbera kamikaze and Gerbera seeker drones – 11,000 units in total." -"In July, they slightly reduced the intensity of their drone strikes and cut production as they reconfigure their manufacturing capacity, with a focus on turbojet-powered Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones. In one of their recent attacks, turbojet-powered drones already accounted for 50% of the total. We now need different interceptors capable of matching their speed, or short-range air defense systems." -"According to estimates by Ukraine's Defense Intelligence, July ranked second after February in the number of Kh-101, Kalibr and Kh-32 cruise missiles launched. In February, the Russians launched 157 such missiles at us, while in July they launched 153." -"As for ballistic and hypersonic missiles – the 9M723 missiles used by the Iskander-M system, the RM-48U missiles launched from S-400 systems, and Zircon missiles – the enemy launched 198 of them in July. That is the highest figure this year." -"In the first seven months of this year, they had already produced 33 Zircon missiles, according to data as of August 3. The same applies to Onyx missiles: as of August 3, they had produced 60 units." -"Overall, across the main types of missile weapons, Russia is currently exceeding its monthly production targets by 110-120%. According to intelligence, Russia’s July production target for Kh-101 missiles was met at 140%, for Kalibr missiles at 111%, and for Kh-35 cruise missiles at 200%. -"Russia’s August production target for Kh-101 missiles is 72 units. The target was the same in July, but they produced more – 87 missiles. For the 3M14 Kalibr, the August target is 26 units. The July target was also 26, but they produced 29." -"According to military intelligence, as of August 5, the stockpile allocated to the Russian military grouping stood at around 130 9M723 missiles. The planned monthly production rate is 60 units. However, in July, they produced 65 instead of the planned 60." -"They are not really drawing down their stockpiles. Almost everything being used now is coming straight off the production line. The only exception is the Kalibr missiles - most of them are currently being allocated to other Russian fleets, since all new Russian warships and submarines are equipped with these systems. In effect, those missiles are going into reserve stockpiles. In addition, our interception rate for Kalibr missiles is nearly 100% when air-defense missiles are available." -The recent Kn-23 missile launch missed its target by 15km. -Regarding the S-400's RM-48U missile, "the enemy has established production of this missile: the August target is about 40 units, while its estimated stockpile is 400 units." -Regarding the Rassvet system, "In March 2026, Russia had already placed 16 satellites into low Earth orbit. More launches will follow to create a constellation of 292 satellites by 2027 and expand it to 924 satellites by 2035." newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/taro…

Redouane Houssaini, presented his Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat today. Secretary-General Dr. Kao congratulated Ambassador Houssaini on his assumption of office and reaffirmed the ASEAN Secretariat’s commitment to further strengthening the ASEAN-Morocco Sectoral Dialogue Partnership established in 2023. The Secretary-General also expressed appreciation for Morocco’s support for ASEAN Community-building efforts. Ambassador Houssaini thanked Secretary-General Dr. Kao for the warm welcome. He looked forward to working closely with ASEAN Member States and the ASEAN Secretariat in further strengthening Morocco’s ties and cooperation with ASEAN during his term of office. Morocco has accredited its first Ambassador to ASEAN since 2010. Ambassador Houssaini succeeds Ambassador Ouadia Benabdellah, who completed his tenure in April 2025.

With 1.2 billion young people worldwide, nearly 89% of them in developing countries, rural youth represent a major opportunity for economic growth. Investments that connect young people to decent jobs, support youth-led enterprises and strengthen participation in decision-making can turn that potential into income, resilience and broader stability. Through its Agribusiness Hubs Programme, IFAD is helping young people build businesses and create jobs. Across nine African countries, the programme has supported more than 8,000 youth-led agribusinesses and helped create over 59,000 jobs. In #Cameroon, the Youth Agropastoral Entrepreneurship Promotion Programme combined fully subsidized education, blended finance and start-up coaching for young entrepreneurs, along with zero-interest start-up loans and productive credit. The programme delivered a 20% increase in food security, a 48% rise in annual income and average annual profits of US$3,000, with 38% annual growth. Ahead of International #YouthDay, the focus is on the opportunities that open up when young people have access to jobs, support to build businesses and a real say in the decisions that shape their futures. کی ہدایت کی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ کاروباری برادری کی جاری ٹیکس اصلاحات پر بڑھتے اعتماد کا خیرمقدم کرتے ہیں. چیئرمین ایف بی آر اور سینئر افسران ہر ماہ کراچی کے ساتھ لاہور میں بھی دو روز قیام کریں. ایف بی آر مقررہ ریونیو ہدف کے حصول کے لیے انفورسمنٹ اقدامات تیز کرے. وزیراعظم نے ایف بی آر کو اسمگلنگ، ٹیکس چوری اور غیر قانونی کاروبار کے خلاف مؤثر انفورسمنٹ جاری رکھنے کی ہدایت کی اور ایف بی آر کی جانب سے چکوال اور صوابی میں سگریٹ سازی کی غیر قانونی فیکٹریوں کے خلاف اقدامات کی پزیرائی کی. وزیراعظم نے ایف بی آر کی تمام حساس پوسٹوں اور محکموں میں اچھی شہرت کے حامل اور ایماندار افسران کے ساتھ ساتھ اسی معیار پر اہلکاروں کی تعیناتی اور ان لینڈ ریونیو کے لیے مجوزہ فیس لیس نظام کی بروقت تکمیل کی بھی ہدایت کی. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ فیس لیس نظام کا مکمل رول آؤٹ 2027 تک یقینی بنایا جائے. اجلاس کو بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ فیس لیس ان لینڈ ریونیو نظام کا پہلا مرحلہ یکم اکتوبر 2026 سے فعال ہوگا. اے آئی اور جدید ٹیکنالوجی پر مبنی فیس لیس نظام ایف بی آر کی حالیہ ڈیجیٹائز یشن اصلاحات کا اہم حصہ ہے.اس نظام میں ٹیکس گوشواروں کے آڈٹ کے لیے نیشنل فیس لیس آڈٹ ونگ اور اسیسمینٹ کے لیے فیس لیس اسیسمینٹ یونٹ شامل ہیں. فیس لیس نظام میں ٹیکس کیسز کا دائرہ اختیار جغرافیائی حدود سے قطع نظر رینڈم بنیادوں پر مختص کیا جائے گا. چیئرمین ایف بی آر نے وزیراعظم کی ہدایت پر ہر ماہ کے پہلے ہفتے کراچی میں قیام اور کاروباری برادری سے ملاقاتوں پر بریفنگ دی. انہوں نے بتایا کہ کراچی میں سات بڑے تجارتی اداروں کے نمائندوں سے ملاقاتیں کیں اور انکے مسائل سنے. کراچی میں قیام کے دوران کاروباری برادری کو درپیش مسائل فوری حل کئے گئے. برآمد کنندگان کے ٹیکس ریفنڈز کے لیے ٹائم باؤنڈ ایس او پیز جاری کیے Today is the birthday of Wolfgang Paul! This physicist was most famous for developing an electromagnetic device known as the Paul trap. Born on this day in 1913, Paul created traps, which are also known as quadrupole ion traps and radiofrequency traps, that use electromagnetic fields to ‘catch’ charged particles so that they may be analysed. These traps, which earned Paul & his colleague Hans Georg Dehmelt the 1989 @NobelPrize in Physics, are an integral part of mass spectrometers, which are large machines used for analysing characteristics of certain atoms, particles and molecules, and chemical structures. These machines are used in our safeguards activities to analyze samples for chemical elements like uranium and plutonium.

Ayurveda's global reach is growing, and the next step is to turn this momentum into wider healthcare integration. Ayush and herbal exports of India have nearly doubled between 2014 and 2023, while Ayurveda-related research now spans nearly 70 countries. NITI Aayog's Strategic Roadmap for Making Ayurveda Global outlines key steps to build greater global trust through: * A Global Ayurveda Register * WHO-aligned qualifications and quality standards * Stronger international research and clinical trials * Ayurveda Centres of Excellence * Greater insurance coverage and medical value travel Together, these measures can help Ayurveda move from growing global interest to wider acceptance and integration into healthcare systems. Explore the roadmap and discover the next chapter of global Ayurveda. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, has authored an opinion piece titled "When a Nation Learns to Care", published in The Statesman, reflecting on the recently released NITI Aayog report "Reimagining Care: Strategies for Empowering Caregivers in Viksit Bharat@2047". The piece emphasises India's changing demographic realities and the importance of building a future-ready caregiving ecosystem through stronger institutions, skilled caregivers, technology-enabled systems, and support for family caregivers. It also underlines the economic potential of the care sector and the opportunity to create dignified livelihoods while strengthening families and communities. दिव्यांग व्यक्तींच्या सक्षमीकरणाला सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या हस्ते आज नागपूर जिल्ह्यातील अस्थिव्यंग व कर्णबधिर दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना निःशुल्क जयपूर फूट साहित्य व सहाय्यक साधनांचे वाटप करण्यात आले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, देशभरात प्रसिद्ध झालेल्या जयपूर फूट आणि इतर दिव्यांग सहाय्यता साहित्यामुळे अनेक दिव्यांगांच्या जीवनात परिवर्तन घडवणे शक्य झाले आहे. कृत्रिम पाय, हात तसेच अन्य कृत्रिम अवयव बसविल्यानंतर दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना दैनंदिन जीवनातील विविध कामे अधिक सुलभपणे करता येतात. या माध्यमातून त्यांच्या जीवनात सकारात्मक परिवर्तन घडवून आणण्यास मदत होते. भगवान महावीर विकलांग सहाय्यता समिती ही 1975 पासून देशात आणि देशाबाहेर दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना सहाय्य करण्याचे उल्लेखनीय कार्य करीत आहे. पंतप्रधान नरेंद्र मोदी यांनी अंध व शारीरिकदृष्ट्या अपंग व्यक्तींना विकलांग न संबोधता दिव्यांग अशी सन्मानजनक ओळख दिली. दिव्यांगांच्या अडचणी शक्य तितक्या कमी करण्यासाठी सरकार प्रयत्नशील आहे. केंद्र व राज्य सरकारच्या विविध योजनांच्या माध्यमातून सातत्याने शिबिरे आयोजित करून दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना आवश्यकतेनुसार श्रवणयंत्र, व्हीलचेअर, अंधांसाठी काठी तसेच इतर साहित्य व उपकरणे उपलब्ध करून देण्यात येत आहेत. राज्य सरकारने दिव्यांग व्यक्तींचे मानधन वाढवून ₹2500 करण्याचा निर्णय घेतला. त्यांना शिक्षण, रोजगार आणि आरोग्याच्या क्षेत्रात सन्मानाची संधी मिळावी यासाठी सरकार काम करत असल्याचे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी नमूद केले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, कर्णबधीर मुलांमध्ये लहान वयातच आवश्यक वैद्यकीय उपचार करण्यात आल्यास त्यांची ऐकण्याची व बोलण्याची क्षमता विकसित होण्यास मदत होऊ शकते. यासाठी 'कॉक्लिअर इम्प्लांट'सारख्या शस्त्रक्रिया महत्त्वाच्या असून, या उपचारासाठी सुमारे ₹6 ते ₹8 लाख खर्च येतो. हा खर्च महाराष्ट्र शासनाच्या माध्यमातून करण्यात येत आहे. भविष्यात राज्यभरात सर्वेक्षण करून विशेषतः 10 वर्षांखालील कर्णबधिर मुले आढळल्यास त्यांच्यावर योग्य वेळी आवश्यक शस्त्रक्रिया केल्या जातील. दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना दरमहा सुमारे ₹20,000 पर्यंत रोजगाराचे साधन उपलब्ध करून देणे, तसेच गृहनिर्माणासह विविध योजनांमध्ये दिव्यांग व्यक्तींना प्राधान्य मिळावे, यासाठीही शासन प्रयत्नशील असल्याचे प्रतिपादन मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी केले. यावेळी मंत्री चंद्रशेखर बावनकुळे, राज्यमंत्री ॲड. आशिष जयस्वाल, आमदार संजय भेंडे, आमदार डॉ. राजीव पोतदार, आमदार कृपाल तुमाने, आमदार मोहन मते, आमदार चरणसिंग ठाकूर, नागपूरच्या महापौर निता ठाकरे, उपमहापौर लीला हाथीबेड, गटनेते नरेंद्र (बाल्या) बोरकर व इतर मान्यवर उपस्थित होते. @narendramodi @Dev_Fadnavis @cbawankule @Ashishjaisw3Adv د آریانا افغان هوايی شرکت می‌گوید، یک انجن بوئینگ ۷۳۷ به ارزش ۲.۳ میلیون دالر امریکایی که از شرکت امریکایی «Global Engine» خریداری شده بود، پس از تکمیل مراحل گمرکی از امریکا به کابل انتقال و از سوی تیم تخنیکی این شرکت روی یک طیارۀ بوئینگ ۷۳۷ نصب شده است. به گفتۀ این شرکت، انتقال این انجن به‌دلیل طی مراحل گمرکی در امریکا با تأخیر مواجه شده بود؛ اما پس از تکمیل این مراحل، انجن به کابل انتقال یافت و تیم تخنیکی آریانا مراحل نصب آن را با موفقیت تکمیل کرد. شرکت آریانا همچنین نوشته است، طیارۀ یادشده حدود دو سال پیش هنگام نشست در میدان هوایی بین‌المللی خوست با یک رویداد مواجه شده بود و پس از آن، تیم تخنیکی این شرکت روند ترمیم آن را در مراحل مختلف انجام داده است. به گفتۀ این شرکت، پس از تکمیل روند ترمیم، انجام آزمایش‌های تخنیکی لازم و اطمینان از رعایت معیارهای مصونیت، این طیارۀ بوئینگ ۷۳۷ برای انجام پروازها آماده خواهد شد. 1. RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat has seen a dramatic transformation in his image. It’s evident he was worried about youth anger towards Modi govt. The first thing he did was to demolish any criticism of Gen Z protesters as anti-national. In my latest #NationalInterest, I argue that RSS is cautioning Modi govt & why Bhagwat’s endorsement of Gen Z has an Indira lesson. 2. Bhagwat has got his loyalists & hard critics confused. The hard ideological base has been thrown by what they see as some increasingly liberal positions he’s taking. This has led to the rise of an Indian “trad” grouping. Sort of like the MAGA to the right of the classical Republicans in the US, although we can’t stretch that comparison too far. 3. Equally, Bhagwat has confused the hard liberal community for whom the BJP, Modi & RSS are a three-in-one entity. For some of them Bhagwat now brings relief. Are these winds of change? Is he cautioning Modi govt? Let me underline first of all, the fundamental ideology & philosophy of the RSS isn’t about to change. What’s on display is political pragmatism in the 13th year of power. 4. Modi govt’s capitulation to Jantar Mantar was rather dramatic & total. And just after senior ministers had said they weren’t like the UPA & their ministers won’t resign under pressure. Kiren Rijiju shared an old clipping of an Indira Gandhi interview to a foreign network justifying the Emergency, hinting at “foreign interference”. The threat to India, she said, was internal & external. 5. She talked about conspiracies, the plans to unleash anarchy, that Morarji Desai had threatened to surround the PM’s house & Parliament. Whether she actually felt so besieged she made the biggest blunder of her public life shall remain a matter of debate. What we do know, though, is there was no other power, a mentor, or a guru to caution her against such misadventure. Bhagwat & the RSS are underlining to us that they fill that gap for their own govt. 6. Read #NationalInterest: theprint.in/national-interes… Watch #NationalInterest: ￼ youtube.com/watch?v=vwob1EDM…

Among the most intriguing artefacts unearthed from the Sindhu-Saraswati Civilization are carefully carved stone boards from 3rd Millennium BCE. These stone boards are marked with geometric grids, often found alongside cubical and elongated dice. Archaeologists have long suggested that these may have served as gaming boards, offering a glimpse into organised leisure and strategic play over 4,500 years ago. While their exact rules remain unknown, some scholars regard them as possible precursors to later Indian board games. The Rig Veda also reflects the enduring place of play in the Indian tradition through its references to dice (akṣa) and games of chance. Whether used for games, counting, or other purposes, these artefacts add another layer to our understanding of the sophisticated social life of the Sindhu-Saraswati Civilization, a legacy whose echoes continue to thrive in Bharat’s living cultural traditions. #SindhuSaraswatiCivilization #AncientPlay #RigVeda #CivilizationalContinuity

//Some conflicts cannot be avoided// Here is a problem no country has solved. 👇 When a government funds frontier technology, the only people who can judge the proposals are usually people already invested in that field. - Take them off the committee and nobody in the room can quite understand the applications. - Keep them on and you get a scandal, a headline. India got that headline last week. - Of the ₹2,192 crore given out in the first round of the new deep-tech fund, 62 per cent went to companies linked to the people who chose them. - Fifteen of the twenty-two firms had ties to seven of the twelve-member committee. Now, nobody argued the companies were bad picks. Agnikul, Ather, Astrome and Manastu Space are firms doing serious work in exactly the areas the fund exists for. The objection was to how they were chosen, not to who was chosen. First the government answered on the expected lines: - Rules written before the first meeting, not after - Any member linked to an applicant must declare it and step out - Two-thirds of the committee needed just to recommend a proposal - The final call rests with a board of secretaries Then, the official in charge said something officials rarely say out loud — Some conflicts cannot be avoided, so you write the rules to keep them from deciding the result. He is right. America has been arguing about this since 1945. Consider the research programme that gave the world radar, penicillin at scale and the atom bomb. - Nearly half its budget went to MIT, Harvard and Caltech. - The presidents of all three sat on the committee handing out the money. The man in charge was Vannevar Bush. - He had been dean of engineering at MIT, - Ran one of America's largest private research funders, - And had co-founded the firm that became Raytheon. Senator Harley Kilgore spent the war saying this was a racket. While he lost the fight over what the postwar agency should look. But his ideas came back anyway, as rules, and those rules are why anyone can check where American research money goes today. Here are the rules America made: - Acting on a decision you have money in became a criminal offence - Exceptions for the expert an agency genuinely cannot replace - A public note naming the person, published before the meeting - Number of such exceptions capped each year and reported to Congress The CIA went further. It built a venture fund and staffed it with working venture capitalists, because nobody else could win good deals in Silicon Valley. A newspaper later found that nearly half its trustees had a financial link to a company the fund had backed. Its portfolio includes Palantir and Anduril. How many would now call seeding those two a mistake? Another agency tried the opposite. After a genuine scandal it banned its scientists from taking drug company money, and five thousand of them had to sell shares. Later, it could not fill its senior posts. The people it needed were the ones it had just shut out. America's Covid vaccine programme, for what it is worth, ran on looser rules than India's. It still worked. Then there is the case that should give both sides pause. Three companies borrowed from the same American programme in the same two years. All three were called politically connected. - Two went bankrupt - One repaid nine years early - One was Tesla None of this makes the worry fake. Recusal mechanism does have a hole too. The circle is small, so when a member steps out of the room, everyone left can work out whose application is on the table. This piece in @SwarajyaMag goes through eighty years of this argument. India has given out just about a fiftieth of this fund. The ₹1 lakh crore behind it is meant to lift an R&D effort still stuck at 0.84 per cent of GDP, against 3.4 per cent in America and 2.6 per cent in China. So the actual questions aren't about the money already spent, but about who sits in the room for the other 98 per cent, and what they disclose on record before they do. महाराष्ट्र की सियासत में पिछले कई दिनों से हलचल है. पीएम मोदी सोमवार को शरद पवार गुट के सांसदों से मुलाकात करेंगे.हालांकि, एनसीपी (एसपी) की कार्यकारी अध्यक्ष सुप्रिया सुले पहले ही यह साफ कर चुकी हैं कि इस बैठक में महाराष्ट्र के मुद्दों पर चर्चा होगी. सुले ने अपने बयान में कहा, 'पीएम मोदी ने सोमवार को एनसीपी सांसदों से मिलने पर सहमति जताई है ताकि सांसद अपने क्षेत्र से जुड़े मुद्दे उनके साथ डिस्कस कर पाएं. चूंकि संसद नहीं चल रही है इसलिए हमने एक मीटिंग की मांग उठाई थी.' लेकिन संभावना जताई जा रही है कि इस बैठक में परिसीमन बिल पर दोनों पार्टियों के बीच चर्चा हो सकती है. विपक्ष ने महिलाओं के आरक्षण को लागू करने से जुड़ी सरकार की प्रस्तावित परिसीमन प्रक्रिया पर चिंता जताई है. इस बैठक से पहले महाविकास अघाड़ी की पार्टियों में एक अजीब से बेचैनी पसरी हुई है. इसमें कांग्रेस और उद्धव ठाकरे की शिवसेना (यूबीटी) शामिल है. ये दोनों ही पार्टियां इंडिया गठबंधन का भी हिस्सा हैं. इस मामले पर शिवसेना (यूबीटी) के राज्यसभा सांसद संजय राउत ने कहा कि उन्होंने सुले से बात की है. उन्होंने कहा,'हम सब एमवीए का हिस्सा हैं. पवार साहब हमारे गाइडिंग फोर्स हैं. एमवीए में कोई कन्फ्यूजन नहीं है, कोई भी एनवीए छोड़कर नहीं जा रहा है.' वहीं दूसरी ओर कांग्रेस का कहना है कि अगर यह बैठक महाराष्ट्र के लिए है तो शुभकामनाएं हैं. पार्टी के नेता विजय वडेट्टीवार ने कहा, 'मुझे नहीं पता कि वे बार-बार मोदी-शाह के दरबार में क्यों जा रहे हैं.' उन्होंने कहा, पता नहीं एनसीपी (एसपी) का परिसीमन बिल पर क्या स्टैंड होगा. कांग्रेस ने एनसीपी (एसपी) से कहा है कि वह पीएम मोदी के साथ बैठक के दौरान इंडिया ब्लॉक का स्टैंड साफ कर दे और बता दे कि प्रस्तावित परिसीमन बिल को महिला आरक्षण के मुद्दे से लिंक नहीं किया जाना चाहिए. #PMModi #Maharashtra #NCP #Meeting | #ZeeNews

An Indian Express front page last Friday had one number flashing prominently — That 62 per cent of the ₹2,192 crore given out in the first round of India's new RDI fund, was to companies linked to the people who chose them. Fifteen of the twenty-two companies had ties to seven of the twelve members on the selection committee. At first glance it looks like a scandal. But read further and you notice that the questions were now over if companies were bad picks. Agnikul, Ather, Astrome, Manastu Space are all serious firms working in exactly the areas the fund was set up for. The objection was to how they were chosen, not to who was chosen. The government answered in usual points — - The rules were written before the first meeting, not after - Any member linked to an applicant has to declare it and step out - A proposal needs two-thirds of the committee just to be recommended - The final decision is taken by a board of secretaries, not by the committee And then the official in charge said something officials rarely say out loud — that in some cases you cannot avoid conflict at all, so you write the rules to make sure it does not decide the result. Now that is not an exclusively Indian problem. The same accusation was once made against the men who ran America's wartime research, the effort that produced radar, penicillin at scale and the atom bomb. Nearly half that budget went to three institutions whose presidents were sitting on the committee that handed out the money. The man in charge had come from MIT, ran one of America's biggest private research funders, and had helped start the company that later became Raytheon. One senator spent the war years making the same argument the Indian Express made last week. He lost the fight over what the new agency should look like. But most of his ideas came back later as rules, and those rules are why anyone can check where American research money goes today. Here is what America ended up doing: - Made it a criminal offence for an official to act on a decision he has money in - Then allowed an exception for an expert the agency genuinely cannot replace - And put a price on that exception, a public note naming the person, published before the meeting There is also a warning in this history. One agency tried to get rid of the problem completely and barred its scientists from taking industry money. Result? It could not fill its senior posts, because the people it wanted were the people it had just shut out. There is also one case that should give both sides pause. Three companies borrowed from the same American programme in the same two years. All three were accused of being politically connected. - Two went bankrupt - The third repaid nine years early - The third was Tesla This piece in @SwarajyaMag goes through eighty years of this argument. The law, the exception, the agency that could not hire, and what Washington eventually decided about judging a fund on one loan versus ten years of them. India has given out about a fiftieth of this fund so far. The ₹1 lakh crore behind it is meant to raise an R&D effort that is still only 0.84 per cent of GDP, against 3.4 per cent in America and 2.6 per cent in China. So the real question is not about the money already spent. It is about who sits in the room for the other 98 per cent, and what they have to declare before they do. سواد رسانه‌ای به توانایی و قدرت دسترسی، تحلیل، ارزیابی و انتقال اطلاعات و پیام‌های رسانه‌ای که می‌توان در چارچوب‌های مختلف چاپی و غیرچاپی عرضه نماید گفته می‌شود. سواد رسانه‌ای یکی از سوادهای دوازده‌گانه است که لزوم یادگیری آن توسط یونسکو و سایر نهادهای بین‌المللی و ملی مسئول در زمینه‌ی آموزش توصیه شده است. همچنان در یک تعریف دیگر، سواد رسانه‌ای مجموعه‌ چشم‌اندازهایی است که فرد برای استفاده از محتوا و پیام‌های رسانه‌ای به‌کار می‌گیرد. سواد رسانه‌ای یک نوع درک متکی بر مهارت است که می‌توان براساس آن انواع رسانه‌ها را از یک‌دیگر تمیز داد و تولیدات رسانه‌ای را از یک‌دیگر تفکیک و شناسایی کرد. سواد رسانه‌ای توانایی بررسی، تجزیه و تحلیل پیام‌هایی که اطلاع‌دهنده و سرگرم‌کننده هستند و هر روز به ما عرضه می‌شوند می‌باشد. همچنان سواد رسانه‌ای توانایی استفاده از مهارت‌های تفکر انتقادی و رابطه‌ی آن با تمام رسانه‌ها است؛ از ویدیوکلیپ‌ها و محیط‌های شبکه‌ای گرفته تا مکان‌های تولیدی در فیلم‌ها و نمایش‌های معنوی در تابلوها. سواد رسانه‌ای طرح سؤال‌های مناسب پیرامون آنچه وجود دارد و دیده می‌شود و توجه کردن به آنچه که دیده نمی‌شود، انگیزه‌ها، ارزش‌ها، مالکیت، سرمایه و آگاه‌بودن از آن که چطور این عوامل بر محتوای پیام‌ها تأثیر می‌گذارند می‌باشد. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/258811

‼️ Royal Navy spy drones used by Britain’s elite special forces secretly sent data to China. ‼️ The cameras on the K3 Scout surveillance drones had components made in China which were secretly transmitting information to a device in the country. The Royal Marines have been using the £12M fleet since March and the Ministry of Defence (MoD) was forced to remove all internet connectivity from the cameras after discovering the breach. The drones were supplied by a major British defense contractor, Kraken Technology Group, which sourced the cameras from a third party who had given assurances about their security. An investigation into the drones revealed that the cameras were transmitting “heartbeat communications” — data to confirm they were online and functioning normally — to an IP address in China. The discovery triggered national security fears that security-cleared staff at the Special Boat Service (SBS) headquarters in Poole, Dorset could have been exposed. The K3 drones made up part of a future defense package offered by the UK to secure the freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Preparations for Britain’s plans in the Gulf had been conducted on the drones. “This is major failure to check origins of components and we have lost confidence in the platform.” There are also concerns that the surveillance drones have been near highly sensitive meetings between senior special forces staff, and that cameras remained active even when the drones were switched off. The revelation comes amid a growing threat from China, despite efforts by the Labour Government to thaw relations with the ruling Chinese Communist Party. A number of supply-chain vulnerabilities have forced the MoD to remove Chinese hardware and cameras from sensitive spaces. The SBS has banned Chinese-made electric cars from its headquarters over similar espionage concerns. Downing Street has begun a diplomatic reset with Beijing through a series of high-profile visits to the country, with the hope of lucrative trade agreements. Earlier this year, the Government approved plans for a Chinese super-embassy at Royal Mint Court in the heart of London, despite concerns about the site’s proximity to sensitive communication lines. MoD: “A routine cyber vulnerability assessment identified an issue affecting a Kraken Unmanned Surface Vessel sub-system used by the Royal Navy. A thorough investigation found no evidence of MoD data or systems being accessed, compromised or transmitted externally. The breach is a major dent to the Navy’s Project Beehive, a programme to develop a combined fleet of uncrewed vessels and traditional warships. The Navy purchased the K3 Scout drones from Kraken as part of the Royal Navy’s surface flotilla. The vessels, operated by the Coastal Forces Squadron and the 47 Commando unit of the Royal Marines, were intended to modernize British war-fighting capabilities and keep pace with adversaries. The K3 Scout model, designed to carry a 600kg payload and operate continuously for 30 days, has also been purchased by the US Special Operations Command and has participated in NATO trials in the Baltic. The UK Government has pledged to accelerate military innovation and make procurement “unashamedly pro-Britain”. But the findings highlight China’s dominance in the supply chain, even when equipment is marketed as British-made. Kraken Technology Group: “We are aware that some third-party, NDAA-compliant cameras had a small number of components originating from outside the UK. 🦁 On World Lion Day, we celebrate India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation. India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to our unwavering commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. From protecting critical habitats to strengthening conservation efforts, India has demonstrated that development and nature conservation can move forward together. From 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025, the steady growth of the Asiatic Lion population reflects the dedication of our forest officials, conservationists, local communities and all those working tirelessly to protect this magnificent species. As we mark World Lion Day, let us reaffirm our resolve to safeguard our natural heritage and ensure that the roar of the Asiatic Lion continues to resonate for generations to come. Video
